GuruConnect Admin Web Portal — Software Requirements Specification

Implementation-ready SRS for the GuruConnect admin portal, split into 51 modules (M0 platform foundation + the 50 requested modules) in the order they should be built. Stack: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript, Node.js 20 + Express 4 + TypeScript, PostgreSQL 16.
Modules 51
PostgreSQL tables 71
Columns (each documented) 1024
Admin API endpoints 436
Permission keys 86 across 5 system roles
Estimated build effort 132–145 developer-days (one full-stack developer, backend + admin UI + tests)

Phase dependency graph

Diagram loads when this page is online…

Ordering notes. The requested phase order is followed, with three places where a module reads data owned by a later one:

  • M30 Parent Subscription and M32 Student Subscription read and act on subscriptions (owned by M41) and transactions (M40). That is why the graph shows Payments before Parents. Either build the M40–M41 backend (tables, services, jobs) right after Phase 6 and the admin screens in order, or build M30/M32 after M41. All migrations can still run up front in numeric order — only the code depends on it.
  • M36 Trust Score uses complaints (M43) for one factor; until M43 ships, that factor scores 100 for everyone.
  • M21 Teacher Analytics and M47 Dashboard show lead and demo numbers that stay at zero until M38–M39 ship.

Running the database

Requires PostgreSQL 16 (tested on PostgreSQL 16.13 (Ubuntu 16.13-0ubuntu0.24.04.1)) with the pgcrypto, citext and pg_trgm extensions (created by migration 000; the database user needs permission to create extensions, or a DBA creates them once).

Option A — one file (local development, CI):

createdb guruconnect
psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d guruconnect -f sql/schema.sql
for f in sql/seed/*.sql; do psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d guruconnect -f "$f"; done

Option B — migrations (recommended for the real project): copy sql/migrations/*.sql into your migration tool (node-pg-migrate in SQL mode, dbmate or Knex raw migrations). They are numbered by module (016_m16_…); numbers are not contiguous because some modules own no tables. Each file is plain SQL and wrapped by the tool in a transaction.

for f in sql/migrations/*.sql; do psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d guruconnect -f "$f"; done

Seeds are idempotent: running them twice changes nothing. The whole schema, all migrations in order and all seeds (twice) were executed on a clean PostgreSQL 16 database while building this pack, and key constraints (one live subscription per user, refund ≤ amount, case-insensitive referral codes, generated case numbers) were smoke-tested.

Confirm before go-live

  • Prices in 003_config.sql are placeholders (Teacher registration ₹499, Institute ₹2,999, Parent ₹299/month or ₹1,999/year, Student ₹199/month or ₹1,499/year, Premium ₹999, Featured ₹1,499, Contact unlock ₹49 — off). Change them in the portal (Module 5) or in the seed.
  • Grievance officer name (IT Rules 2021) — contact.grievance_officer is [TO CONFIRM].
  • GSTIN, legal entity name and address for invoices (Module 40) — not in the seed; add as settings.
  • Safety keywords for complaint triage (complaints.safety_keywords) — starter list only; review with your trust & safety lead, including regional-language terms.
  • Support phone and email, app store versions, allowed banner domains.
  • Referral rewards (₹100/₹100 learner, ₹200 teacher, institute program off) and trust score weights (20/10/20/25/15/10).

00 · Engineering Conventions (read first)

Every module in this pack follows the rules on this page. A module document only repeats a rule when it overrides it.

3. API conventions

  • Base path: /api/v1/admin for the admin portal. Public mobile endpoints mentioned in modules live under /api/v1/app and are out of scope except where an admin change must be visible to the app.
  • Naming: plural nouns, kebab-case paths, camelCase JSON. Database columns are snake_case; the repository layer maps them.
  • IDs: UUID v4 strings everywhere. Human-friendly codes (e.g. GC-T10241) are for display and search only.
  • Money: integer paise (amountPaise: 49900). The UI formats with Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', {style:'currency', currency:'INR'}).
  • Time: timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC in JSON (2026-09-26T11:30:00.000Z). The UI renders in the admin's time zone (default Asia/Kolkata). Date-only fields use YYYY-MM-DD.
  • Success envelope:
    { "data": { … } }
{ "data": [ … ], "meta": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 20, "total": 342, "totalPages": 18 } }
  • Error envelope:
    { "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED", "message": "Some fields need attention.", "details": [ { "path": "amountPaise", "message": "Must be 0 or more" } ], "requestId": "7d1c…" } }
  • Status codes: 200 read/update, 201 create, 202 accepted (async job), 204 delete, 400 malformed JSON, 401 unauthenticated, 403 missing permission, 404 not found (also for soft-deleted rows), 409 conflict, 413 payload too large, 415 wrong content type, 422 validation, 429 rate limited, 500 unexpected, 502 gateway (Razorpay/S3/FCM) error.
  • Updates: PATCH with only the changed fields. Rows that several admins may edit (profiles, settings, configs, reviews) require the header If-Match: <updatedAt of the row as read>. A mismatch returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with the current row, and the UI shows "Someone else changed this. Reload to see their changes."
  • State changes use action endpoints (POST /teachers/:id/approve), never a generic PATCH status, so each transition can validate, audit and notify.
  • Idempotency: POST endpoints that create money movements or send messages accept Idempotency-Key (UUID). The key and response are stored in Redis for 24 hours.

Standard error codes

Code HTTP When
AUTH_REQUIRED 401 No or malformed access token
AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED 401 Access token expired — client must call refresh
AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS 401 Wrong email or password
AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED 423 Too many failed logins; details.lockedUntil
AUTH_ACCOUNT_DISABLED 403 Admin disabled
AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID 401 Refresh token missing, expired, revoked or reused
AUTH_LINK_EXPIRED 410 Reset or invite link invalid, used or expired
FORBIDDEN 403 Missing permission; details.required lists the key
NOT_FOUND 404 Row missing or soft-deleted
VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Zod validation failed; details has field errors
CONFLICT_DUPLICATE 409 Unique rule violated (maps PG error 23505)
CONFLICT_STATE 409 Action not allowed from the current status; details.currentStatus
CONFLICT_IN_USE 409 Delete blocked because other rows reference it; details.references
VERSION_CONFLICT 409 If-Match mismatch
RATE_LIMITED 429 Too many requests; Retry-After header
FILE_TOO_LARGE / FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED 413 / 415 Upload checks
GATEWAY_ERROR 502 Razorpay, S3, SES or FCM failed
IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH 422 Idempotency-Key reused with a different request body
INVALID_SIGNATURE 400 Webhook HMAC check failed (public webhook receivers only)
QUERY_TIMEOUT 503 Report query exceeded statement_timeout (15 s); suggest narrowing filters or exporting
INTERNAL_ERROR 500 Anything else (logged with requestId)

4. Pagination, sorting, filtering, search

  • Offset pagination (default for admin tables): ?page=1&pageSize=20. pageSize allowed values 10, 20, 50, 100; default 20; max 100. Response meta has page, pageSize, total, totalPages.
  • Cursor pagination for append-only, high-volume lists (audit logs, timelines, notification recipients, raw events): ?limit=50&cursor=<opaque>; meta.nextCursor is null on the last page. The cursor encodes (created_at, id).
  • Totals: for tables that can exceed 100,000 rows, total is an estimate from pg_class.reltuples when no filter is applied; meta.totalIsEstimate: true.
  • Sorting: ?sort=createdAt:desc,fullName:asc. Each list endpoint declares an allow-list of sortable fields; anything else returns 422. A unique tiebreaker (id) is always appended.
  • Filters: plain query params, repeated for multi-select: ?status=pending&status=under_review&cityId=<uuid>&createdFrom=2026-09-01&createdTo=2026-09-30. Date ranges are inclusive and interpreted in Asia/Kolkata.
  • Search: ?q= (2–100 chars, trimmed). Matching rules are defined per module (usually ILIKE prefix on codes/emails/phones + pg_trgm similarity on names).
  • The React DataTable keeps page, sort, filters and q in the URL query string so views are shareable and survive refresh.

5. Authentication and RBAC in every request

Middleware order: requestId → helmet/cors → pino-http → rateLimit → authenticate → loadPermissions → validate → handler → audit → errorHandler.

  • authenticate verifies the access JWT (see Module 1), loads req.admin = { id, email, isSuperAdmin, sessionId } and rejects disabled admins or revoked sessions (session id checked against a Redis deny-list).
  • requirePermission('teachers.approve') checks the admin's effective permissions (union of all roles), cached in Redis perm:<adminId> for 5 minutes and busted on any role or assignment change. Super admins pass every check.
  • The React app reads GET /auth/me → permissions[], hides navigation items and buttons the admin cannot use (<Can permission="teachers.approve">), and still handles 403 from the API.

6. Soft delete

  • Tables with deleted_at are soft-deleted: UPDATE … SET deleted_at = now(), deleted_by = :adminId.
  • Every repository query adds deleted_at IS NULL unless the endpoint explicitly supports ?includeDeleted=true (super admin only).
  • Unique indexes are partial (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) so a deleted name can be reused.
  • Deleting a master record that is referenced by live rows returns 409 CONFLICT_IN_USE; the UI offers "Deactivate instead".
  • Restores: POST /<resource>/:id/restore where a module says so.

7. Audit logging (all admin actions)

  • Every successful state-changing admin request writes one audit_logs row in the same database transaction as the change (helper audit(tx, {...})). If the audit insert fails, the change rolls back.
  • action naming: <entity>.<verb> in past tense, e.g. teacher.approved, payment_config.published, admin.role_assigned.
  • old_values / new_values contain only changed fields. Never log password hashes, tokens, OTPs, full Aadhaar/PAN numbers or document URLs; the helper strips keys matching /password|token|secret|aadhaar_number|pan_number|signed_url/i.
  • Read access to sensitive data is audited too: unmasking a document, viewing full phone numbers, exporting reports (*.unmasked, *.pii_viewed, report.exported).
  • Security events (login success/failure, lockout, password reset, token reuse) are logged with actor_type = 'admin' or 'system'.
  • Each module lists its audit events in section 19. Module 0 provides the audit log viewer.

8. Validation rules (global)

  • Strings are trimmed; empty strings become null for optional fields.
  • Names: 2–100 chars, letters, spaces, ., ', -; no emoji.
  • Email: RFC 5322 basic, max 254, stored lower-case (citext).
  • Phone: Indian mobile in E.164 ^\+91[6-9]\d{9}$ unless the module allows other countries.
  • URLs: https:// only, max 2,048.
  • UUID params are validated before hitting the database (bad UUID → 404, not 500).
  • Money: integer paise, 0 ≤ value ≤ 10,00,00,000 (₹10 lakh) unless stated.
  • Text areas: max length per field; HTML is stripped server-side; Markdown is sanitised on render.
  • Enumerations: validated against the same CHECK lists as the database (shared enums in packages/shared).

Human-readable codes. Codes shown to people come from PostgreSQL sequences through column defaults, so the application never generates them: teachers.public_code GC-T10001… (seq_teacher_code), institutes.public_code GC-I2001…, parents.public_code GC-P50001…, students.public_code GC-S50001…, leads.public_code LD-100001…, transactions.public_code TXN-7000001…, complaints.case_number CS-1001…. Sequences are never reset; gaps after rolled-back transactions are expected.

9. File uploads

  1. Client calls POST /api/v1/admin/files/presign with { purpose, fileName, mimeType, sizeBytes, checksumSha256 }.
  2. API validates purpose-specific rules (documents: PDF/JPEG/PNG ≤ 10 MB; images: JPEG/PNG/WebP ≤ 5 MB), creates a files row with status = 'pending' and returns a presigned PUT URL (5-minute expiry) and fileId.
  3. Client uploads directly to S3/R2, then calls POST /files/:id/confirm. API checks the object exists, size and checksum match, queues a virus scan, sets status = 'uploaded'.
  4. Private files are only served through GET /files/:id/url which returns a 60-second signed URL and audits access for documents.

10. Background jobs (BullMQ)

Queue Schedule Used by
payment-config-activate every minute M5 — activates scheduled fee versions
trust-recalc on event + nightly 02:00 IST M36, M37
analytics-rollup hourly (today) + nightly 01:00 IST M21, M47
subscription-lifecycle every 15 minutes M30, M32, M41 — expiry, grace, reminders
referral-release hourly M42 — releases held rewards
notifications-send on demand / scheduled M46
report-export on demand M48–M50
banner-status every 5 minutes M44 — activates / expires banners
cleanup nightly M1 sessions and reset tokens, M0 soft-deleted files

Jobs run as actor_type = 'system' in the audit log.

11. Security baseline

  • HTTPS only, HSTS 1 year. Admin portal on its own domain (admin.guruconnect.in), not linked from the public site, behind Cloudflare with bot protection.
  • CORS allow-list: the admin origin only. Cookies: Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/admin/auth.
  • CSRF: the refresh endpoint checks Origin and a double-submit X-CSRF-Token; all other endpoints use the Bearer header (not cookies).
  • Rate limits (Redis): login 5/min per IP+email, forgot password 3/hour per email, general API 300/min per admin, exports 10/hour per admin.
  • Secrets in AWS Secrets Manager / environment; never in the repo.
  • PII: phone numbers and emails of app users are masked (+91 98XXX XX210) unless the admin has users.pii; unmask requests are audited.
  • Aadhaar handling: store only masked numbers and an HMAC hash for duplicate detection; never store full Aadhaar numbers. Document files are private and encrypted at rest (SSE-S3 / R2 default).
  • Dependencies scanned in CI (npm audit, Dependabot); OWASP ASVS L2 as the checklist.

12. UI conventions (admin web)

  • Layout: left sidebar (collapsible below 1080 px, drawer below 720 px), sticky top bar with global search, content max-width 1600 px.
  • Shared components (build once in the first module that needs them): PageHeader, DataTable (server-side pagination/sort, row selection, column visibility, sticky header, CSV export button), FilterBar, SearchInput (300 ms debounce), StatusBadge, ConfirmDialog (typed-reason variant), Drawer, FormField, MoneyInput (₹ ↔ paise), DateRangePicker, EntityPicker (async select), FileUploader (presign flow), Timeline, EmptyState, ErrorState, Can (permission gate), AuditTrail (entity history panel).
  • Every list page has: loading skeleton, empty state, error state with retry, and keeps filters in the URL.
  • Every destructive or money-affecting action uses ConfirmDialog; actions that affect users (reject, suspend, publish price) require a reason.
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA, visible focus, keyboard-operable tables and dialogs, labels on every input.

13. Definition of done (per module)

  1. Migration(s) applied; Kysely types regenerated.
  2. Zod schemas in packages/shared; API routes with permission checks, validation and audit.
  3. API tests covering every row of the module's Error Scenarios table.
  4. React pages and components with loading/empty/error states and permission gating.
  5. Audit events visible in the entity's AuditTrail panel.
  6. Seed data updated if the module adds permissions or reference data.

01 · Data Model

71 tables in PostgreSQL 16. Every entity table uses a uuid primary key (gen_random_uuid()); join tables use composite keys (e.g. role_permissions (role_id, permission_id)), one-to-one extensions use the parent id (admin_profiles, trust_scores) and daily rollups use the date (daily_platform_stats, teacher_daily_stats). All tables use timestamptz timestamps and snake_case names. Soft-deletable tables carry deleted_at / deleted_by with partial unique indexes WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Full column definitions are in each module file (sections 9–10) and in sql/schema.sql.

Relationship diagrams by domain

Each diagram shows the tables owned by that domain and the tables they reference. References to admins (created_by, decided_by, …) and files are left out of the diagrams to keep them readable; they are listed in the foreign-key table below.

audit_logs M00 Append-only record of every admin action and security event. Never updated or deleted by the application. 15

Conventions recap

  • Money: bigint paise, never numeric floats in JS. Ratings: numeric(2,1) / numeric(3,2); scores: numeric(5,2).
  • Enums: text + CHECK (… IN (…)) rather than PostgreSQL enum types, so values can be added in a migration without ALTER TYPE locks.
  • Versioned config (payment configurations, referral settings, trust weights, institute ratings): rows are never edited after activation; a partial unique index guarantees one active and one draft per key.
  • Append-only logs (audit_logs, *_logs, *_history, complaint_actions): no updated_at, never updated or deleted by the app; revoke UPDATE, DELETE from the app role on them.
  • updated_at is maintained by the set_updated_at() trigger and doubles as the optimistic-locking version sent in If-Match.

02 · API Index

All 436 admin endpoints. Base URL /api/v1/admin unless the path says otherwise. Every endpoint requires a valid access token and the listed permission (checked by requirePermission() middleware). Envelope, errors, pagination and idempotency rules are in 00-conventions.md.

M00 Platform Foundation (Audit Logs, Files, App Users)

Method Path Permission Description
GET /audit-logs audit_logs.read List audit entries (cursor pagination)
GET /audit-logs/:id audit_logs.read One entry with full old/new values
GET /audit-logs/entity/:entityType/:entityId read permission of that entity's module History of one record
POST /files/presign any authenticated admin Create a pending file and return an upload URL
POST /files/:id/confirm uploader or super admin Confirm the upload finished

GET /search any authenticated admin Global search across entities

03 · RBAC Matrix

Permissions are module.action keys. An admin's effective permissions are the union of their roles' permissions; Super Admin has all keys and cannot be edited. Roles other than Super Admin can be edited or cloned in Module 2; this matrix is the seeded default (sql/seed/001_rbac.sql). Keys marked sensitive require a reason on use, are highlighted in the audit log, and some require re-authentication within 5 minutes.

Roles

Role Code Purpose
Super Admin super_admin Full access (Sameer Bhaiya). Cannot be edited or deleted.
Operations Admin operations_admin Runs day-to-day marketplace data: masters, teachers, institutes, users, leads, CMS.
Verification Admin verification_admin Reviews teacher and institute documents, evaluates institutes, watches trust scores.
Finance Admin finance_admin Owns pricing, payments, refunds, subscriptions and referral rewards.
Support Admin support_admin Handles reviews, complaints and user support.

04 · React App Structure

Admin web app: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript, React Router 6 (data routers), TanStack Query for server state, TanStack Table, React Hook Form + Zod (schemas shared with the API from packages/shared), Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (Radix), Recharts, dnd-kit, CodeMirror 6 (blog editor).

Folder layout

apps/admin-web/src/
  app/                 router.tsx, providers.tsx (QueryClient, Auth, Theme), AppShell.tsx
  lib/                 api.ts (fetch wrapper: envelope, 401 → refresh → retry, If-Match), money.ts, dates.ts (IST), permissions.ts
  components/ui/       shadcn primitives (Button, Dialog, Sheet, Tabs, Table, Badge, Tooltip, Toast…)
  components/shared/   DataTable, FilterBar, SearchInput, Pagination, StatusBadge, ConfirmDialog, ReasonDialog, EmptyState,
                       PermissionGate, MoneyCell, DateCell, UserChip, FileViewer, AuditTrail, KpiCard, PageHeader
  features/<module>/   pages/, components/, api/<module>.api.ts (query keys + hooks), schemas.ts (re-exports shared Zod)
  styles/              tokens.css (light/dark), tailwind.css

App shell

  • Top bar: global search (Module 0 /search, ⌘K), notifications bell (export ready, approvals waiting), profile menu (Module 3).
  • Sidebar (items hidden when the admin lacks the read permission): Dashboard · Approvals (Teachers, Institutes) · Teachers · Institutes · Parents · Students · Reviews · Trust scores · Leads · Demos · Payments (Transactions, Refunds, Subscriptions, Reconciliation) · Referrals · Complaints · CMS (Banners, Blogs, Notifications) · Reports (Revenue, Teachers, Institutes, Exports) · Masters (Locations, Classes, Subjects, Boards, Modes, Categories) · Settings (Global, Pricing, Referral rules, Roles & permissions, Admins, Audit log).
  • Route guard: <RequirePermission keys={[...]}> wraps each route; unauthorised routes render a 403 page, not a redirect loop.
  • Data pattern: list pages keep filters, sort and page in the URL query string (shareable links); detail pages use drawers for quick views and full pages for workflows.
  • Mutations: every state change goes through a dialog that collects the reason where required, sends If-Match, shows a toast naming the result, and invalidates the affected queries.

  • Read replica for reports and dashboard; later a columnar analytics store fed by CDC.

  • Public status of verification and ratings as structured data for SEO.

Module 0 · Platform Foundation (Audit Logs, Files, App Users)

Phase 0 · Platform Foundation · Depends on: none — build first · Owns tables: audit_logs, files, app_users · Build estimate: 3–4 days

1. Module Overview

Shared plumbing every other module uses: the append-only audit log and its viewer, the file-upload service (presigned S3/R2 uploads), and the app_users identity table that parents, students, teachers and institute staff hang off. It also delivers the Express skeleton (middleware chain, error handler, pagination helpers) and the React shell (layout, router, DataTable, FilterBar, PageHeader, ConfirmDialog, Can).

2. Business Purpose

  • Sameer Bhaiya must be able to answer "who changed this, when and why" for any record. The audit log is the single source for that and for security investigations.
  • Teachers and institutes upload identity documents. These must be stored privately, served only through short-lived signed links, and every view of an original document must be traceable.
  • Admins need one consistent way to look up any mobile user (parent, student, teacher, institute staff) regardless of role.

3. User Stories

  • As Super Admin, I want to filter the audit log by admin, module, action and date so that I can investigate a disputed change.
  • As Super Admin, I want to open any record's history from its detail page so that I see every change in context.
  • As any admin, I want to upload an image or document once and reuse its id in forms so that uploads are fast and never pass through our API server.
  • As a Verification Admin, I want document links to expire quickly so that leaked URLs are useless.
  • As a developer, I want a standard error, pagination and audit helper so that every module behaves the same.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-0.1 Audit helper. audit(tx, { action, module, entityType, entityId, oldValues, newValues, reason }) inserts into audit_logs inside the caller's transaction. Actor, IP, user agent and request id are taken from the request context (AsyncLocalStorage). Sensitive keys are stripped (see Conventions §7). The helper computes a diff so only changed keys are stored.

FR-0.2 Audit viewer. List with filters, cursor pagination and a detail drawer that shows a side-by-side old/new JSON diff. Export to CSV through Module 48's export service (report_type = 'audit_logs').

FR-0.3 Entity history. GET /audit-logs/entity/:entityType/:entityId powers the reusable AuditTrail panel on every detail page (latest 50, "Load more").

FR-0.4 File presign. POST /files/presign validates purpose, MIME type and size against the purpose rules table below, creates a files row (pending) and returns a presigned PUT URL valid for 5 minutes. Object key pattern: {purpose}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{fileId}.{ext}.

Purpose Bucket Allowed types Max size
teacher_document, institute_document, complaint_evidence private application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png 10 MB
admin_avatar, banner_image, blog_image, category_icon, subject_icon, notification_image public image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp 5 MB
report_export private text/csv, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet 200 MB (system only)

FR-0.5 File confirm. POST /files/:id/confirm issues HeadObject, verifies size and SHA-256 (from S3 checksum), sets status = 'uploaded' and enqueues a ClamAV scan job; infected files become quarantined and are never served.

FR-0.6 Signed URL. GET /files/:id/url returns a 60-second signed GET URL for private files (public files return the CDN URL). For purposes teacher_document and institute_document the caller needs teacher_documents.unmask / institute_documents.unmask, and an audit row file.viewed is written.

FR-0.7 App user lookup. GET /app-users and GET /app-users/:id give a role-agnostic view (type, status, created, last active) used by global search and by support. Contact fields are masked unless the admin holds users.pii.

FR-0.8 Global search. GET /search?q= searches teachers, institutes, parents, students, leads (by code), transactions (by code or gateway id) and complaints (by case number) in parallel, returning at most 5 hits per type. Each hit carries type, id, title, subtitle, route. Results are filtered by the admin's read permissions.

FR-0.9 Cleanup job. Nightly: files pending for more than 24 h are deleted from storage and marked deleted; soft-deleted files older than 30 days are purged from storage.

5. Validation Rules

  • purpose must be one of the table above; mimeType must match the purpose; sizeBytes 1 … max; fileName 1–255 chars, sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9._-].
  • checksumSha256 optional, 64 hex chars when present.
  • Audit filters: from/to ISO dates, to ≥ from, range ≤ 366 days; action and module max 80 chars; actorId UUID.
  • Global search q: 2–100 chars after trim.

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /audit-logs audit_logs.read List audit entries (cursor pagination)
GET /audit-logs/:id audit_logs.read One entry with full old/new values
GET /audit-logs/entity/:entityType/:entityId read permission of that entity's module History of one record
POST /files/presign any authenticated admin Create a pending file and return an upload URL
POST /files/:id/confirm uploader or super admin Confirm the upload finished
GET /files/:id/url depends on purpose (see FR-0.6) Short-lived download URL
DELETE /files/:id uploader or super admin Soft-delete an unused file (409 if referenced)
GET /app-users any of parents.read, students.read, teachers.read, institutes.read Role-agnostic user list
GET /app-users/:id same as above One user with linked profile ids
GET /search any authenticated admin Global search across entities

9. PostgreSQL Tables

audit_logs

Append-only record of every admin action and security event. Never updated or deleted by the application.

CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  actor_type text NOT NULL CHECK (actor_type IN ('admin','system','app_user')), -- Who performed the action
  actor_id uuid, -- admins.id / app_users.id; NULL for system jobs (no FK so logs survive deletions)
  actor_email citext, -- Snapshot of the actor's email at the time of the action
  action text NOT NULL, -- Dotted event name, e.g. teacher.approved, payment_config.published
  module text NOT NULL, -- Module slug, e.g. teachers, payment_config
  entity_type text, -- Table or aggregate name, e.g. teachers
  entity_id uuid, -- Primary key of the affected row
  old_values jsonb, -- Changed fields before the action (sensitive fields removed)
  new_values jsonb, -- Changed fields after the action (sensitive fields removed)
  reason text, -- Free-text reason entered by the admin, when the action requires one
  ip_address inet, -- Client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first trusted hop)
  user_agent text, -- Client user agent, truncated to 512 chars
  request_id uuid, -- Correlation id from the X-Request-Id header
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- When the action happened
);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_created_at ON audit_logs (created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_entity ON audit_logs (entity_type, entity_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_actor ON audit_logs (actor_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_logs_module_action ON audit_logs (module, action, created_at DESC);

files

Metadata for every uploaded object stored in S3 / Cloudflare R2. Binary content never touches PostgreSQL.

CREATE TABLE files (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  storage_provider text NOT NULL DEFAULT 's3' CHECK (storage_provider IN ('s3','r2')), -- Object store in use
  bucket text NOT NULL, -- Bucket name
  object_key text NOT NULL, -- Full object key, e.g. teachers/<uuid>/aadhaar/<uuid>.pdf
  original_name text NOT NULL, -- File name as uploaded (sanitised, max 255)
  mime_type text NOT NULL, -- Validated MIME type
  size_bytes bigint NOT NULL CHECK (size_bytes > 0), -- File size in bytes
  checksum_sha256 text, -- Hex SHA-256 reported by the client and verified after upload
  visibility text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'private' CHECK (visibility IN ('private','public')), -- private = signed URLs only (documents); public = CDN (banners, blog images)
  purpose text NOT NULL, -- Why it was uploaded, e.g. teacher_document, banner_image, admin_avatar
  uploaded_by_type text NOT NULL CHECK (uploaded_by_type IN ('admin','app_user','system')), -- Uploader kind
  uploaded_by_id uuid, -- Uploader id (polymorphic, no FK)
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','uploaded','quarantined','deleted')), -- pending until the upload is confirmed and virus-scanned
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last updated
  deleted_at timestamptz -- Soft delete; object is removed from storage by a cleanup job after 30 days
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_files_object ON files (bucket, object_key);
CREATE INDEX idx_files_purpose ON files (purpose, created_at DESC);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_files_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON files FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

app_users

Login identity for every mobile app account (parent, student, teacher, institute staff). Role profiles hang off this table.

CREATE TABLE app_users (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  user_type text NOT NULL CHECK (user_type IN ('parent','student','teacher','institute_staff')), -- Primary role chosen at sign-up
  phone text, -- E.164 mobile number, e.g. +919845014210
  phone_verified_at timestamptz, -- Set after OTP verification
  email citext, -- Email address
  email_verified_at timestamptz, -- Set after email verification
  full_name text NOT NULL, -- Display name
  auth_provider text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'otp' CHECK (auth_provider IN ('otp','password','google','apple')), -- First sign-in method
  account_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (account_status IN ('active','suspended','banned','deactivated')), -- Suspended and banned users cannot sign in
  suspended_reason text, -- Shown to support staff, not to the user
  suspended_at timestamptz, -- When suspended
  last_active_at timestamptz, -- Last authenticated request (updated at most every 5 minutes)
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last updated
  deleted_at timestamptz -- Soft delete (account deletion request); PII is anonymised by a job after 30 days
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_app_users_phone ON app_users (phone) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND phone IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_app_users_email ON app_users (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND email IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_app_users_type_status ON app_users (user_type, account_status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_app_users_name_trgm ON app_users USING gin (full_name gin_trgm_ops);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_app_users_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON app_users FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

Migration file: sql/migrations/000_m00_platform_foundation_extensions_helpers_audit_logs_files_app_users.sql

12. Indexing Strategy

Index Table Kind Definition
idx_audit_logs_created_at audit_logs btree (created_at DESC)
idx_audit_logs_entity audit_logs btree (entity_type, entity_id, created_at DESC)
idx_audit_logs_actor audit_logs btree (actor_id, created_at DESC)
idx_audit_logs_module_action audit_logs btree (module, action, created_at DESC)
uq_files_object files unique (bucket, object_key)
idx_files_purpose files btree (purpose, created_at DESC)
uq_app_users_phone app_users unique (phone) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND phone IS NOT NULL
uq_app_users_email app_users unique (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND email IS NOT NULL
idx_app_users_type_status app_users btree (user_type, account_status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
idx_app_users_name_trgm app_users gin USING gin (full_name gin_trgm_ops)
  • audit_logs is append-only and grows fastest; indexes serve the four access paths: recent first, by entity, by actor, by module+action. When it passes ~20 M rows convert it to a range-partitioned table by month (PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)) and keep 24 months online, older partitions archived to S3 (Parquet).
  • app_users phone/email uniques are partial so deleted accounts free their identifiers; the trigram index powers name search.

  • AuditDiffDrawer — two-column JSON diff with changed keys highlighted.

16. Filters

Audit logs: actor (admin picker), module (select), action (text/select of known actions), entity type, entity id, date range (default last 7 days), actor type (admin/system/app_user).

17. Search Capabilities

  • Global search: codes (GC-T…, LD-…, TXN-…, CS-…) match exactly (case-insensitive); phone numbers match on the last 10 digits; emails match by prefix; names by trigram similarity ≥ 0.3 ordered by similarity.
  • Audit logs: no free text; use filters (free-text search over JSON is intentionally not offered).

18. Pagination Requirements

  • Audit logs: cursor pagination, limit 50 (max 200), ordered created_at DESC, id DESC.
  • Entity history: latest 50, cursor for more.
  • App users: offset, default 20.

Scenario HTTP Code Message shown
Unsupported MIME for purpose 415 FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED "This file type isn't allowed here. Use PDF, JPG or PNG."
File larger than limit 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE "Files must be 10 MB or smaller."
Confirm before upload finished 409 CONFLICT_STATE "Upload not found in storage yet. Try again."
Checksum mismatch 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "The file was corrupted during upload. Upload it again."
File quarantined by virus scan 409 CONFLICT_STATE "This file failed a security scan and can't be used."

S3/R2 unavailable 502 GATEWAY_ERROR "File storage is not responding. Try again in a minute."

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

  • Partition audit_logs monthly; ship to a data lake (S3 + Athena) for long-term queries.
  • Move virus scanning to a Lambda triggered by S3 events.
  • Add OpenSearch for global search when entity counts pass a few million; keep Postgres as the source of truth.
  • Consider WORM storage (S3 Object Lock) for audit archives to satisfy compliance audits.

22. Security Considerations

  • Audit writes are transactional and immutable at the DB-grant level.
  • Presigned URLs are single-object, short-lived, and bound to Content-Type; public bucket objects are immutable (new key per upload).
  • Private bucket blocks all public access; S3 server-side encryption on; bucket policy denies non-TLS requests.
  • File names are never used as object keys (prevents path tricks); Content-Disposition: attachment on private downloads.

Module 1 · Authentication System

Phase 1 · Foundation · Depends on: M0 · Owns tables: admins, admin_sessions, password_reset_tokens · Build estimate: 4–5 days

1. Module Overview

Email-and-password sign-in for the admin portal with short-lived JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens stored in an httpOnly cookie, forgot/reset password by email, account lockout, and a session manager where an admin can see and sign out their devices.

2. Business Purpose

The admin portal can approve teachers, change prices and suspend accounts. A compromised admin account is the highest-impact risk on the platform, so authentication must be strict (lockout, rotation with reuse detection, instant revocation) while staying simple for a small team.

3. User Stories

  • As an admin, I want to sign in with my email and password so that I can use the portal.
  • As an admin, I want to stay signed in for a working week on my own laptop ("Keep me signed in") so that I am not asked to log in all day.
  • As an admin, I want to reset a forgotten password through an emailed link so that I can regain access without calling Sameer.
  • As an admin, I want to see where I am signed in and sign out other devices so that I can secure my account.
  • As Super Admin, I want an account to lock after repeated failed logins so that passwords cannot be brute-forced.
  • As Super Admin, I want changing a password to sign the admin out everywhere else so that a leaked session dies immediately.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-1.1 Login. POST /auth/login with email and password.

  1. Rate limit: 5 attempts per minute per (IP, email) and 20 per hour per IP.
  2. Load admin by email (deleted_at IS NULL). If not found, run a dummy Argon2 verify (constant time) and return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
  3. If status = 'disabled' → AUTH_ACCOUNT_DISABLED. If locked_until > now() → AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED with lockedUntil.
  4. Verify Argon2id (m=19456, t=2, p=1). On failure increment failed_login_count; at 5 set locked_until = now() + 15 min and status = 'locked', send a "someone tried to sign in" email; return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
  5. On success reset the counter, set status = 'active' if it was locked, update last_login_at/ip, create an admin_sessions row, return the access token in the body and set the refresh cookie.

FR-1.2 Tokens.

  • Access token: JWT RS256, 15-minute lifetime, claims sub (admin id), sid (session id), sa (is super admin), pwd (password_changed_at epoch), iat, exp, iss = guruconnect-admin, aud = admin-portal. Kept in memory in the React app (never localStorage).
  • Refresh token: 256-bit random, base64url, stored only as SHA-256 in admin_sessions.refresh_token_hash. Cookie gc_admin_rt, HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/admin/auth. Session lifetime 7 days (30 with "Keep me signed in"), sliding by refresh but never past expires_at.

FR-1.3 Refresh with rotation. POST /auth/refresh reads the cookie, hashes it and finds an unrevoked, unexpired session. It issues a new refresh token, stores the new hash and moves the old hash to previous_token_hash, and returns a new access token.

  • Reuse detection: if the presented hash matches a previous_token_hash (already rotated), revoke every session in that token_family with reason token_reuse, audit auth.token_reuse_detected and email the admin.
  • Parallel requests: a 10-second grace window allows the immediately previous token once (handles two tabs refreshing at the same moment).

FR-1.4 Authentication middleware. Verifies JWT signature and claims, then checks Redis revoked_sid:<sid> (set when a session is revoked, TTL 15 min) and pwd ≥ admin's password_changed_at. Disabled admins are rejected even with a valid token.

FR-1.5 Logout. POST /auth/logout revokes the current session (revoked_reason = 'logout'), clears the cookie and writes revoked_sid. POST /auth/logout-all revokes every session of the admin.

FR-1.6 Forgot password. POST /auth/forgot-password always returns 202 (no account enumeration). If an active admin exists, create a token (32 random bytes, stored hashed, 30-minute expiry, previous unused tokens for that admin invalidated) and email https://admin.guruconnect.in/reset-password?token=…. Limit 3 requests per hour per email.

FR-1.7 Reset password. POST /auth/reset-password with token and new password. Validates token (exists, unused, unexpired), sets new hash, password_changed_at = now(), marks token used, revokes all sessions (password_changed), clears lockout, and emails a confirmation. Also used for invite tokens (purpose = 'invite', 72 hours) created by Module 2 — accepting an invite sets status = 'active'.

FR-1.8 Current admin. GET /auth/me returns profile basics, roles and the effective permission keys (Module 2) for the React app.

FR-1.9 Sessions. GET /auth/sessions lists the admin's active sessions (device label, IP, last used, current flag). DELETE /auth/sessions/:id revokes one of the admin's own sessions. With sessions.revoke_any, DELETE /admins/:adminId/sessions revokes all sessions of another admin.

FR-1.10 Password policy. 12–128 chars; at least three of: lower, upper, digit, symbol; not equal to the email or name; not in the top-100k breached list (bundled bloom filter or HIBP k-anonymity API); not one of the last 5 passwords (store last 5 hashes in a password_history jsonb on admins — optional, see scalability).

FR-1.11 Bootstrap. CLI npm run admin:create -- --email … --name … --super creates the first super admin with an invite token printed once. There is no public sign-up.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
email required, valid email, ≤ 254, lower-cased
password (login) required, 1–128 chars (policy is not re-checked at login)
newPassword policy in FR-1.10; must differ from current password
token required, 43-char base64url
rememberMe boolean, default false
sessionId UUID, must belong to the caller

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
POST /auth/login public (rate limited) Sign in, returns access token + sets refresh cookie
POST /auth/refresh refresh cookie + CSRF header Rotate refresh token, return new access token
POST /auth/logout authenticated Revoke current session
POST /auth/logout-all authenticated Revoke all own sessions
POST /auth/forgot-password public (rate limited) Email a reset link (always 202)
POST /auth/reset-password public (token) Set a new password with a reset or invite token
GET /auth/reset-password/validate public (token) Check a token before showing the form
GET /auth/me authenticated Current admin, roles, permissions
GET /auth/sessions authenticated Own active sessions
DELETE /auth/sessions/:id authenticated (own session) Sign out one device
DELETE /admins/:adminId/sessions sessions.revoke_any Force sign-out another admin everywhere

9. PostgreSQL Tables

admins

Admin web portal accounts. Every admin action is attributed to a row here.

CREATE TABLE admins (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  email citext NOT NULL, -- Login email, unique among non-deleted admins
  password_hash text NOT NULL, -- Argon2id hash (never returned by any API)
  full_name text NOT NULL, -- Display name, 2–100 chars
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('invited','active','locked','disabled')), -- invited = must set password; locked = too many failed logins; disabled = access removed
  is_super_admin boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Bypasses permission checks; at least one active super admin must always exist
  failed_login_count smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Consecutive failed logins; reset on success
  locked_until timestamptz, -- Login blocked until this time after 5 failures
  last_login_at timestamptz, -- Last successful login
  last_login_ip inet, -- IP of the last successful login
  password_changed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Used to invalidate tokens issued before a password change
  mfa_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Reserved for TOTP (future)
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin who created this account
  updated_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin who last updated this account
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last updated
  deleted_at timestamptz, -- Soft delete
  deleted_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id) -- Admin who deleted this account
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_admins_email ON admins (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_admins_status ON admins (status) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_admins_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON admins FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

admin_sessions

One row per signed-in device. Holds the hashed refresh token used to mint new access tokens.

CREATE TABLE admin_sessions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Session id; also the "sid" claim in access tokens
  admin_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admins(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Session owner
  refresh_token_hash text NOT NULL, -- SHA-256 of the current refresh token (the raw token is only in the httpOnly cookie)
  token_family uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Rotation family; reuse of an old token revokes the whole family
  previous_token_hash text, -- Hash of the token that was rotated out, used for reuse detection
  ip_address inet, -- IP at sign-in
  user_agent text, -- Browser user agent at sign-in
  device_label text, -- Parsed label, e.g. "Chrome on Windows"
  last_used_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last refresh
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, -- Absolute expiry (7 days, or 30 with "keep me signed in")
  revoked_at timestamptz, -- Set on logout, password change or forced sign-out
  revoked_reason text CHECK (revoked_reason IN ('logout','logout_all','password_changed','token_reuse','admin_forced','expired','account_disabled')), -- Why it was revoked
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Sign-in time
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_admin_sessions_token ON admin_sessions (refresh_token_hash);
CREATE INDEX idx_admin_sessions_admin_active ON admin_sessions (admin_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_admin_sessions_prev_token ON admin_sessions (previous_token_hash) WHERE previous_token_hash IS NOT NULL;

password_reset_tokens

Single-use, 30-minute tokens for the forgot-password and invite flows.

CREATE TABLE password_reset_tokens (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  admin_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admins(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Account being reset
  token_hash text NOT NULL, -- SHA-256 of the emailed token
  purpose text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reset' CHECK (purpose IN ('reset','invite')), -- invite tokens live 72 hours
  expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL, -- Expiry
  used_at timestamptz, -- Set when consumed; a used token can never be reused
  requested_ip inet, -- IP that requested the reset
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Created
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_password_reset_tokens_hash ON password_reset_tokens (token_hash);
CREATE INDEX idx_password_reset_tokens_admin ON password_reset_tokens (admin_id, created_at DESC);

Migration file: sql/migrations/001_m01_authentication_system.sql

Index Table Kind Definition

20. Error Scenarios

Scenario HTTP Code Message shown
Wrong email or password 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS "Email or password is incorrect."
Account locked 423 AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED "Too many attempts. Try again after {time}."
Account disabled 403 AUTH_ACCOUNT_DISABLED "Your access has been removed. Contact the Super Admin."
Too many login requests 429 RATE_LIMITED "Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again."
Access token expired 401 AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED (silent refresh)
Refresh cookie missing/expired/revoked 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID "Your session ended. Sign in again."
Refresh token reused 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID "For your security we signed you out everywhere. Sign in again."
Missing/invalid CSRF header on refresh 403 FORBIDDEN "Session check failed. Reload the page."
Reset token invalid, used or expired 410 AUTH_LINK_EXPIRED "This link has expired. Request a new one."
New password fails policy 422 VALIDATION_FAILED Field-level checklist
New password equals current 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Choose a password you haven't used before."
Revoking a session that isn't yours 404 NOT_FOUND "Session not found."

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

  • Add TOTP MFA (mfa_enabled, secret encrypted with KMS, backup codes) and make it mandatory for roles holding sensitive permissions.
  • SSO with Google Workspace (OIDC) once the team grows; keep password login for break-glass super admin.
  • Password history table if the policy needs "not last 5".
  • Move JWT signing keys to KMS with rotation (kid header, JWKS endpoint).
  • IP allow-listing per role (e.g., Finance only from office IPs).

22. Security Considerations

  • Argon2id with per-hash salt; constant-time comparisons; generic error for unknown email.
  • Refresh token only in an httpOnly cookie scoped to the auth path; access token only in memory (XSS cannot persist it).
  • Refresh rotation with reuse detection; revocation effective within one request through the Redis deny-list.
  • CSRF protection on the cookie-authenticated refresh endpoint (Origin check + double-submit token).
  • Lockout plus notification emails for suspicious activity; all security events audited.
  • Nightly job deletes expired sessions older than 30 days and used/expired reset tokens older than 7 days.

Module 2 · Roles & Permissions

Phase 1 · Foundation · Depends on: M0, M1 · Owns tables: roles, permissions, role_permissions, admin_roles · Reads: admins · Build estimate: 4 days

1. Module Overview

Role-based access control for the admin portal. Five system roles are seeded (Super Admin, Operations Admin, Finance Admin, Verification Admin, Support Admin). Super Admin can create custom roles, edit which permissions a role grants, invite admins, assign one or more roles to each admin, and disable admins. Every API route declares the permission it needs.

2. Business Purpose

GuruConnect will grow from one admin (Sameer Bhaiya) to a team. Permissions must be granular enough that a Finance Admin can change prices without seeing Aadhaar documents, and a Support Admin can suspend an abusive parent without touching pricing — and changes must take effect immediately without a deploy.

3. User Stories

  • As Super Admin, I want to invite a new admin by email and give them a role so that they can start work the same day.
  • As Super Admin, I want to see a permission matrix for a role and tick or untick permissions so that I control exactly what each role can do.
  • As Super Admin, I want to create a custom role (e.g., "City Launch Admin") by copying an existing role so that I can tailor access quickly.
  • As Super Admin, I want to disable an admin who left so that they lose access immediately.
  • As an admin, I want the portal to show only the menus and buttons I can use so that I am not confused by errors.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-2.1 Permission catalogue. Permissions are defined in code (packages/shared/permissions.ts) and synced into permissions by the seed on every deploy (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). Admins cannot create permission keys. Keys removed from code are deleted from the table and from role_permissions.

FR-2.2 System roles. Seeded with is_system = true (matrix in each module's Permissions section). super_admin cannot be renamed, deleted or have permissions removed; it implicitly has every permission (checked through admins.is_super_admin, which is set when the role is assigned). Other system roles can have permissions edited but cannot be deleted.

FR-2.3 Custom roles. Create with name, description and permission list (or "copy from role"). Code is generated from the name (city_launch_admin), unique. Delete (soft) only when no admin holds the role; otherwise CONFLICT_IN_USE listing holders.

FR-2.4 Edit role permissions. PUT /roles/:id/permissions replaces the full set (diffed server-side). Requires If-Match. On success: audit with added/removed keys, bust the Redis permission cache of every admin holding the role, and publish a permissions.changed event so open browser tabs refetch /auth/me (via a 60-second poll of /auth/me?etag= or SSE).

FR-2.5 Admins. List, view, invite, edit name, assign/unassign roles, disable, re-enable, soft-delete.

  • Invite: creates admins row (status = 'invited', random unusable password hash), assigns roles, creates an invite token (Module 1, 72 h) and emails it. Re-send invite regenerates the token.
  • Disable: status = 'disabled', revoke all sessions, write revoked_sid entries.
  • Guard rails: an admin cannot disable, delete or remove super_admin from themselves; the system refuses any change that would leave zero active super admins.

FR-2.6 Effective permissions. Union of permissions of all assigned roles (SELECT DISTINCT p.key …). Cached in Redis perm:<adminId> (5 min). requirePermission(...keys) passes when the admin holds any of the keys given; requireAllPermissions when all are needed.

FR-2.7 Sensitive permission warning. Granting a permission with is_sensitive = true shows a confirmation listing the sensitive keys and requires a reason, stored in the audit log.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
role.name 3–50 chars, unique (case-insensitive) among live roles
role.description ≤ 250 chars
permissionKeys array of known keys, 0–200 items, no duplicates
admin.email valid email, unique among live admins
admin.fullName 2–100 chars
roleIds 1–5 UUIDs of live roles
reason required 5–500 chars when sensitive permissions are granted, or when disabling/deleting an admin

9. PostgreSQL Tables

roles

Named bundles of permissions. System roles are seeded and cannot be deleted.

CREATE TABLE roles (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  code text NOT NULL, -- Stable machine name, e.g. super_admin, finance_admin
  name text NOT NULL, -- Display name, e.g. Finance Admin
  description text, -- What this role is for
  is_system boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Seeded roles; name/permissions of super_admin are immutable
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Creator
  updated_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Last editor
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last updated
  deleted_at timestamptz, -- Soft delete (custom roles only, and only when no admin holds it)
  deleted_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id) -- Who deleted it
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_roles_code ON roles (code) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_roles_name ON roles (lower(name)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_roles_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON roles FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

permissions

Catalogue of permission keys. Seeded from code; admins cannot create permissions.

CREATE TABLE permissions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  key text NOT NULL, -- Dotted key checked by the API, e.g. teachers.approve
  module text NOT NULL, -- Module slug used to group the permission matrix UI
  description text NOT NULL, -- What the permission allows
  is_sensitive boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Sensitive permissions (payments, roles, document unmasking) are highlighted in the UI
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Created
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_permissions_key ON permissions (key);
CREATE INDEX idx_permissions_module ON permissions (module);

role_permissions

Which permissions each role grants.

CREATE TABLE role_permissions (
  role_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Role
  permission_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES permissions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Permission granted
  granted_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin who granted it
  granted_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- When granted
  PRIMARY KEY (role_id, permission_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_role_permissions_permission ON role_permissions (permission_id);

admin_roles

Which roles each admin holds. An admin may hold several roles; effective permissions are the union.

CREATE TABLE admin_roles (
  admin_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admins(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Admin
  role_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Role held
  assigned_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Who assigned it
  assigned_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- When assigned
  PRIMARY KEY (admin_id, role_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_admin_roles_role ON admin_roles (role_id);

Migration file: sql/migrations/002_m02_roles_permissions.sql

  • Scope roles by city or institute (admin_role_scopes table with scope_type, scope_id) when regional teams arrive.
  • Time-boxed access grants (auto-expire a role assignment).
  • Approval workflow for sensitive permission grants (two-person rule).
  • Export the permission matrix as CSV for compliance reviews.

22. Security Considerations

  • Deny by default: a route without requirePermission fails a CI lint rule (eslint-plugin-guruconnect/require-permission).
  • Permission checks happen server-side on every request; the UI gating is convenience only.
  • Cache invalidation on every role/assignment change so revoked access takes effect within one request.
  • Two-super-admin minimum recommended; system prevents zero.

Module 3 · Admin Profile Management

Phase 1 · Foundation · Depends on: M0, M1 · Owns tables: admin_profiles · Reads: admins, files · Build estimate: 1–2 days

1. Module Overview

Lets each admin view and edit their own profile (display name, phone, designation, avatar, time zone, theme, notification preferences) and change their password while signed in.

2. Business Purpose

Names and photos make the audit trail and case assignments readable ("Anjali approved this"), and personal time zone/theme settings make the portal comfortable for daily use.

3. User Stories

  • As an admin, I want to upload a profile photo so that teammates recognise my actions in timelines.
  • As an admin, I want to change my password from my account page so that I can rotate it regularly.
  • As an admin, I want to pick dark mode and my time zone so that dates and the UI suit me.
  • As an admin, I want to choose which email alerts I get so that my inbox stays useful.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-3.1 View profile. GET /me/profile returns admins basics + admin_profiles (created lazily with defaults on first read).

FR-3.2 Edit profile. PATCH /me/profile updates display name, phone, designation, time zone, locale, theme and notification preferences. fullName (on admins) can also be edited here. Email changes are not self-service (Super Admin edits in Module 2) to protect the login identity.

FR-3.3 Avatar. Upload via Module 0 presign with purpose = admin_avatar, then PUT /me/profile/avatar { fileId }. The API checks the file is uploaded, owned by the caller and an image; the old avatar file is soft-deleted. DELETE /me/profile/avatar removes it. The UI crops to a square (client-side) before upload; server generates 64/128/256 px variants through the CDN image resizer.

FR-3.4 Change password. POST /me/change-password { currentPassword, newPassword, signOutOtherSessions }. Verifies current password (counts toward lockout like login), applies the Module 1 policy, updates hash and password_changed_at, revokes other sessions (always when signOutOtherSessions is true; default true) and keeps the current session by re-issuing tokens.

FR-3.5 Notification preferences. Keys: email_digest (daily queue summary at 9 AM), queue_alerts (email when a queue item breaches SLA), security_alerts (always on, not editable).

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
fullName 2–100 chars
displayName 2–40 chars, optional
phone E.164, optional
designation ≤ 80 chars
timezone valid IANA zone (checked against Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone'))
locale one of en-IN, hi-IN
theme light, dark, system
notificationPrefs object with boolean email_digest, queue_alerts only
avatar fileId UUID of an uploaded image file created by the caller, purpose admin_avatar
currentPassword / newPassword as Module 1; new ≠ current

Method Path Permission Description
GET /me/profile authenticated Own profile
PATCH /me/profile authenticated Update own profile (If-Match)
PUT /me/profile/avatar authenticated Set avatar from an uploaded file
DELETE /me/profile/avatar authenticated Remove avatar
POST /me/change-password authenticated Change own password

Module 4 · Global Settings

Phase 2 · Configuration · Depends on: M0, M1, M2 · Owns tables: system_settings · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Overview

A typed key–value settings store for platform-wide values: platform name and tagline, support contact details, grievance officer, legal URLs (terms, privacy, refunds), app version gates (latest/minimum Android and iOS versions, maintenance mode) and operational limits (max children per parent, max teachers per institute). Settings flagged public are served to the mobile app.

2. Business Purpose

These values change more often than code ships (a new support number, a forced app update after a security fix, a new terms URL). Admins must change them safely without a deploy, with validation per value type and a full history.

3. User Stories

  • As Super Admin, I want to update the support email and phone so that users reach the right team.
  • As Super Admin, I want to raise the minimum Android version so that users on an insecure build must update.
  • As Operations Admin, I want to switch on maintenance mode during a database migration so that users see a friendly screen.
  • As a mobile developer, I want one public endpoint with all public settings and an ETag so that the app can cache them.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-4.1 Grouped settings. Settings are grouped (general, contact, legal, app_versions, limits). The list endpoint returns them grouped, ordered by key.

FR-4.2 Typed validation. Each setting has a value_type that drives both the server validation and the React input:

value_type Validation Input
string 1–200 chars text
number integer, per-key min/max (table below) number
boolean true/false switch
url https URL text with open-link button
email email text
phone E.164 phone input
semver ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$ text
json must match the per-key Zod schema JSON editor

Per-key extra rules: limits.parent_max_children 1–5; limits.institute_max_teachers 1–200; limits.review_min_chars 10–200; app.*_min_version must be ≤ the matching *_latest_version.

FR-4.3 Bulk save. PATCH /settings accepts a map of key → value for one group, validates all, and saves them in one transaction (all or nothing). Requires If-Match equal to the latest updated_at among the submitted keys.

FR-4.4 Maintenance mode. Turning app.maintenance_mode on requires a reason and a confirmation. While on, the public endpoint returns maintenance: true and the mobile API returns 503 for all non-auth routes (admin portal unaffected).

FR-4.5 Public settings. GET /api/v1/app/settings (mobile, unauthenticated) returns only is_public = true settings as a flat object, cached in Redis and with ETag/Cache-Control: max-age=300. Saving any public setting purges the cache.

FR-4.6 Read-only settings. is_editable = false rows (e.g., values managed by deploys) are shown greyed out with an explanation; attempts to change them return 409.

FR-4.7 History. Each setting's detail shows its audit history (Module 0 entity history on system_settings).

New settings are only added by migrations/seeds, never through the UI, so every key has code that reads it.

5. Validation Rules

See FR-4.2. Additionally: value must be present for every submitted key; unknown keys → 422; reason (5–500 chars) required for app.* keys and for maintenance mode.

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /settings settings.read All settings grouped
GET /settings/:key settings.read One setting with metadata
PATCH /settings settings.update Save several settings of one group atomically

Module 5 · Dynamic Payment Configuration

Phase 2 · Configuration · Depends on: M0, M1, M2 · Owns tables: payment_configurations, payment_configuration_history · Build estimate: 5 days

1. Module Overview

Admin control over every fee the platform charges: Teacher Registration, Institute Registration, Parent Subscription (monthly, yearly), Student Subscription (monthly, yearly), Premium Teacher listing, Featured Teacher listing and Contact Unlock. Each fee can be switched on or off and priced; changes are saved as versions with an effective date, published immediately or scheduled, and every change is kept in a version history. No code change is needed to change what users pay.

2. Business Purpose

The monetisation strategy is not final. Sameer Bhaiya needs to test prices, run launch offers, or make the platform free for a segment — safely. Versioning guarantees that (a) a user is charged exactly the price shown when they started checkout, (b) past invoices can always be explained, and (c) a mistaken change can be rolled back.

3. User Stories

  • As Finance Admin, I want to change the parent yearly price from ₹1,999 to ₹1,799 starting 1 November so that the Diwali offer starts automatically.
  • As Super Admin, I want to switch the teacher registration fee off during launch so that teachers join free.
  • As Finance Admin, I want to see every past price of a fee with who changed it and why so that I can explain invoices.
  • As Finance Admin, I want to preview what users will see before publishing so that I don't publish a mistake.
  • As Super Admin, I want to cancel a scheduled price change so that I can reverse a decision before it takes effect.
  • As the mobile app, I want one endpoint that tells me which fees are on and their prices so that purchase screens are always correct.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

Concepts. A fee is identified by fee_code. Each fee has versions. Exactly one version is active at a time (partial unique index), zero or more are scheduled (future effective_from), at most one is draft. Versions are immutable once published — changes create a new version.

State machine

draft ──publish(now)──▶ active ──(newer version activates)──▶ superseded
draft ──publish(future)──▶ scheduled ──(scheduler at effective_from)──▶ active
scheduled ──cancel──▶ cancelled
draft ──discard──▶ (deleted)

FR-5.1 List fees. GET /payment-configs returns one card per fee: current active version, next scheduled version (if any), draft (if any), and 30-day usage (captured transactions count and revenue from Module 40, when available).

FR-5.2 Create/edit draft. PUT /payment-configs/:feeCode/draft creates or replaces the fee's single draft by copying the active version and applying changes (is_enabled, amount_paise, gst_inclusive, gst_rate_bps, billing_period, validity_days, trial_days, name, description). Draft saves are autosaved from the UI (debounced 1 s).

FR-5.3 Preview. GET /payment-configs/:feeCode/draft/preview returns the user-facing price card (price, per-month equivalent for yearly plans, GST split, trial text, enabled state) and an impact summary: number of live subscriptions on the current version (they keep their price until renewal), number of users currently in checkout (open Razorpay orders < 30 min).

FR-5.4 Publish. POST /payment-configs/:feeCode/draft/publish { effectiveFrom, reason }:

  1. effectiveFrom omitted or ≤ now + 1 min → immediate: in one transaction set the current active version to superseded with effective_to = now(), set the draft to active with effective_from = now(), version = max+1.
  2. effectiveFrom in the future (≤ 365 days) → draft becomes scheduled. Only one scheduled version per fee at a time; publishing another schedule requires cancelling the existing one first.
  3. Write payment_configuration_history (published or scheduled) and the audit row.
  4. Purge the Redis cache pricing:v1 and publish a pricing.changed event (mobile gets fresh prices on next fetch; open checkout sessions keep the price captured in their Razorpay order).

FR-5.5 Quick toggle. POST /payment-configs/:feeCode/toggle { enabled, reason } publishes a new version immediately that differs only in is_enabled. Use for "switch the fee off now".

FR-5.6 Scheduler. BullMQ job payment-config-activate runs every minute: for each scheduled version with effective_from ≤ now(), in a transaction supersede the active version and activate the scheduled one; history action activated with changed_by = NULL. Idempotent (row lock FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).

FR-5.7 Cancel schedule. POST /payment-configs/versions/:id/cancel { reason } — only scheduled versions.

FR-5.8 Roll back. POST /payment-configs/versions/:id/restore { reason, effectiveFrom? } copies an old version into a new draft and publishes it (a restore is always a new version, history stays linear).

FR-5.9 Price resolution (used by Modules 30, 32, 40, 41 and the mobile API). resolveFee(feeCode, at = now()) returns the version with status IN ('active','scheduled') AND effective_from ≤ at AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > at) ordered by effective_from DESC LIMIT 1. The resolved version id and amount are stored on the transaction when the Razorpay order is created, so the price a user saw is the price they pay.

FR-5.10 Disabled fee behaviour (contract for the mobile app and Modules 30/32/41).

Fee off App behaviour
TEACHER_REGISTRATION Registration skips payment; teacher goes straight to the verification queue
INSTITUTE_REGISTRATION Same for institutes
PARENT_/STUDENT_SUBSCRIPTION_* Both periods off → membership screens hidden, users get free_access subscriptions (Module 41); one period off → only that plan hidden
PREMIUM_TEACHER / FEATURED_TEACHER Purchase buttons hidden; existing paid periods run to their end
CONTACT_UNLOCK No pay-per-contact option

FR-5.11 GST split. base = round(amount / (1 + rate)) when gst_inclusive; otherwise amount is the base and GST is added at checkout. Rounding to the nearest paisa; the split is stored on the transaction.

FR-5.12 Public pricing endpoint. GET /api/v1/app/pricing returns every fee's resolved active version (enabled flag, amount, period, trial days, display name), cached in Redis for 60 s and purged on publish.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
feeCode one of the 9 codes
amountPaise integer 0 … 1,00,00,000 (₹1,00,000); 0 allowed only if isEnabled is false or the fee is a trial-only plan
isEnabled boolean
gstInclusive boolean
gstRateBps 0, 500, 1200, 1800 or 2800
billingPeriod must match the fee: registration → yearly or one_time; *_MONTHLY → monthly; *_YEARLY → yearly; PREMIUM/FEATURED → per_30_days; CONTACT_UNLOCK → per_use
validityDays required unless per_use; 1–1,095; monthly ≈ 28–31, yearly 365/366, per_30_days = 30
trialDays 0–90; only for subscription fees (else must be 0)
effectiveFrom ISO timestamp, not in the past (> now − 1 min), ≤ now + 365 days
reason required, 5–500 chars, for publish, toggle, cancel, restore
name 3–60 chars; description ≤ 200
Price change guard a change of more than ±50 % in one version requires confirmLargeChange: true

9. PostgreSQL Tables

payment_configurations

One row per version of each fee. The app charges whichever version is active at payment time.

CREATE TABLE payment_configurations (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key (one per version)
  fee_code text NOT NULL CHECK (fee_code IN ('TEACHER_REGISTRATION','INSTITUTE_REGISTRATION','PARENT_SUBSCRIPTION_MONTHLY','PARENT_SUBSCRIPTION_YEARLY','STUDENT_SUBSCRIPTION_MONTHLY','STUDENT_SUBSCRIPTION_YEARLY','PREMIUM_TEACHER','FEATURED_TEACHER','CONTACT_UNLOCK')), -- Which fee this row prices
  version integer NOT NULL CHECK (version > 0), -- 1, 2, 3… per fee_code
  name text NOT NULL, -- Display name shown to users, e.g. Parent Membership (Monthly)
  description text, -- Short description shown on the pricing screen
  is_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- false = fee switched off; the app hides the purchase and skips the payment step
  amount_paise bigint NOT NULL CHECK (amount_paise >= 0), -- Price in paise (₹499 = 49900)
  currency char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INR', -- ISO 4217 currency
  gst_inclusive boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- true = amount already includes GST
  gst_rate_bps integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1800 CHECK (gst_rate_bps BETWEEN 0 AND 2800), -- GST in basis points (18% = 1800)
  billing_period text NOT NULL CHECK (billing_period IN ('one_time','monthly','quarterly','yearly','per_30_days','per_use')), -- How often it is charged
  validity_days integer CHECK (validity_days IS NULL OR validity_days > 0), -- Access length after payment (NULL for per_use)
  trial_days integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (trial_days BETWEEN 0 AND 90), -- Free trial before first charge (subscriptions only)
  effective_from timestamptz NOT NULL, -- When this version starts applying
  effective_to timestamptz, -- Set automatically when a newer version becomes effective
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','scheduled','active','superseded','cancelled')), -- Lifecycle of the version
  change_reason text, -- Required note explaining the change
  published_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin who published
  published_at timestamptz, -- When published
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Creator of the draft
  updated_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Last editor
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last updated
  CONSTRAINT ck_payment_config_period CHECK (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > effective_from)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_payment_config_version ON payment_configurations (fee_code, version);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_payment_config_one_active ON payment_configurations (fee_code) WHERE status = 'active';
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_payment_config_one_draft ON payment_configurations (fee_code) WHERE status = 'draft';
CREATE INDEX idx_payment_config_lookup ON payment_configurations (fee_code, effective_from DESC) WHERE status IN ('active','scheduled');
CREATE TRIGGER trg_payment_configurations_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON payment_configurations FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

payment_configuration_history

Immutable change log for payment configurations (create, edit, publish, cancel, activate, supersede).

CREATE TABLE payment_configuration_history (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  payment_configuration_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES payment_configurations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Version that changed
  fee_code text NOT NULL, -- Denormalised for fast filtering
  action text NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('created','updated','published','scheduled','activated','superseded','cancelled','enabled','disabled')), -- What happened
  old_values jsonb, -- Fields before the change
  new_values jsonb, -- Fields after the change
  reason text, -- Admin's reason
  changed_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- NULL when the scheduler activated a version
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- When
);
CREATE INDEX idx_payment_config_history_fee ON payment_configuration_history (fee_code, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_payment_config_history_config ON payment_configuration_history (payment_configuration_id, created_at DESC);

12. Indexing Strategy

Index Table Kind Definition
uq_payment_config_version payment_configurations unique (fee_code, version)
uq_payment_config_one_active payment_configurations unique (fee_code) WHERE status = 'active'
uq_payment_config_one_draft payment_configurations unique (fee_code) WHERE status = 'draft'
idx_payment_config_lookup payment_configurations btree (fee_code, effective_from DESC) WHERE status IN ('active','scheduled')
idx_payment_config_history_fee payment_configuration_history btree (fee_code, created_at DESC)
idx_payment_config_history_config payment_configuration_history btree (payment_configuration_id, created_at DESC)
  • uq_payment_config_one_active and uq_payment_config_one_draft enforce the state rules in the database, so two admins publishing at once cannot create two active versions (the second transaction fails and the API returns 409).
  • idx_payment_config_lookup serves resolveFee (fee_code + effective_from DESC).
  • History is read by fee and by version.

Separating payment_config.edit (drafts) from payment_config.publish allows a maker–checker flow: a Finance Admin can prepare a draft that the Super Admin publishes.
