9. PostgreSQL Tables

trust_score_weights

Versioned factor weights. Exactly one active version; weights must add up to 100.

CREATE TABLE trust_score_weights (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  version integer NOT NULL, -- Version number
  weights jsonb NOT NULL, -- {"aadhaar":20,"pan":10,"certificates":20,"reviews":25,"complaints":15,"profile_completeness":10}
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','active','superseded')), -- Lifecycle
  change_reason text, -- Why weights changed
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Creator
  activated_at timestamptz, -- When activated
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Created
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_trust_score_weights_version ON trust_score_weights (version);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_trust_score_weights_active ON trust_score_weights (status) WHERE status = 'active';

trust_scores

Current trust score per teacher with its factor breakdown.

CREATE TABLE trust_scores (
  teacher_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES teachers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- One row per teacher
  score numeric(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Final 0–100 score shown to users
  computed_score numeric(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (computed_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Score from the formula before any override
  aadhaar_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (aadhaar_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100
  pan_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (pan_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100
  certificate_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (certificate_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100
  review_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (review_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100 (Bayesian-smoothed rating)
  complaint_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 100 CHECK (complaint_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100 (100 = no upheld complaints)
  completeness_score smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (completeness_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Factor 0–100
  weights_version integer NOT NULL, -- trust_score_weights.version used
  inputs jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb, -- Raw inputs, e.g. {"published_reviews":42,"avg_rating":4.8,"upheld_complaints_12m":0}
  is_overridden boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Admin override active
  override_score numeric(5,2) CHECK (override_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- Manual score
  override_reason text, -- Required with an override
  override_expires_at timestamptz, -- Override ends automatically
  overridden_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Who overrode
  is_frozen boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Frozen during an investigation; recalculation is skipped
  calculated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Last calculation
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Updated
);
CREATE INDEX idx_trust_scores_score ON trust_scores (score DESC);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_trust_scores_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON trust_scores FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

Module 37 · Trust Score History

Phase 10 · Trust Score Engine · Depends on: M36 · Owns tables: trust_score_logs · Reads: trust_scores, teachers · Build estimate: 1–2 days

1. Module Overview

An immutable history of every trust score change: old and new score, factor breakdown after the change, what triggered it (document decision, review, complaint, profile update, weights change, override, schedule, freeze) with a link to the cause, and the admin if manual. Shown as a chart and a timeline per teacher, plus a platform-wide change log.

2. Business Purpose

When a teacher asks "why did my score drop from 91 to 84?", support must answer with evidence. History also lets admins audit manual overrides and measure the impact of weight changes.

3. User Stories

  • As Support Admin, I want a teacher's score chart with events on it so that I can explain a drop.
  • As Super Admin, I want to list all manual overrides in the last month so that I can review them.
  • As Verification Admin, I want to see the biggest score drops this week so that I can check for problems.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-37.1 Writing. Module 36's publishScore() inserts a log row whenever the published score changes by ≥ 0.01 or a manual action happens (freeze, override, etc.), in the same transaction as the trust_scores update.

FR-37.2 Teacher history. GET /trust-scores/:teacherId/history?from&to — series of (date, score) and events with trigger, cause link (review id, complaint case, document), note, admin.

FR-37.3 Global log. GET /trust-score-logs?triggerType&adminId&minDelta&from&to — cross-teacher list; minDelta (absolute change) helps find big movers.

FR-37.4 Retention. Logs are kept 36 months; older rows are aggregated to monthly snapshots (trigger_type = 'scheduled' kept only at month-end) by a yearly job.

5. Validation Rules

from/to dates (≤ 366 days span); triggerType from the CHECK list; minDelta 0–100; adminId UUID.

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /trust-scores/:teacherId/history trust_scores.history Score series and events for a teacher
GET /trust-score-logs trust_scores.history Global change log
GET /trust-score-logs/:id trust_scores.history One log entry with breakdown

Module 38 · Lead Management

Phase 11 · Leads · Depends on: M16, M22, M26, M28, M29, M31 (M40 adds the unlock-transaction FK) · Owns tables: leads · Reads: teachers, institutes, app_users, parent_children, subjects, classes, institute_teachers, transactions · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

A lead is an enquiry, call-back request or demo request sent by a parent or student to a teacher or an institute. The mobile API creates leads; this module gives admins a searchable list across the platform, the full detail of a lead with its timeline, the ability to correct status, mark spam and add internal notes, and the response-time metrics that feed teacher analytics (Module 21) and the dashboard (Module 47).

2. Business Purpose

Leads are the marketplace's core outcome — a family reaching a teacher. Support needs to trace a lead when a parent says "the teacher never called back", operations needs response-rate and conversion numbers, and trust & safety needs to spot spam and harassment patterns early.

3. User Stories

  • As Support Admin, I want to find a lead by its code or the parent's phone so that I can answer "did my request reach the teacher?".
  • As Operations Admin, I want to see teachers with many unanswered leads so that I can nudge or de-rank them.
  • As Support Admin, I want to mark a lead as spam so that it stops counting against the teacher's response rate.
  • As Operations Admin, I want conversion from lead to demo to enrolment by city so that I can see where the funnel leaks.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-38.1 Lifecycle (set by the mobile API; admins can correct).

From To Actor Notes
— new requester public_code = LD- + 6-digit sequence (seq_lead_code); push + SMS to receiver
new viewed receiver opens it first view does not set first_response_at
new / viewed contacted receiver taps Call/WhatsApp or replies sets first_response_at
contacted converted receiver or requester marks enrolled; or a demo outcome enrolled sets closed_at
any open declined receiver, with decline_reason sets closed_at, first_response_at if null
any open closed system after 30 days without activity, or requester sets closed_at
any spam admin (leads.manage) or 3 receiver reports excluded from metrics; requester gets a strike (5 strikes in 30 days → Module 43 auto-complaint)

Admins may move a lead to any status except new; spam → previous status is allowed within 7 days ("Not spam").

FR-38.2 Limits (enforced by the mobile API, shown here for support). Requester: max 10 new leads per day, max 1 open lead per (requester, target, subject). Contact unlock: when the CONTACT_UNLOCK fee is enabled and the requester has no live subscription, the phone number is shared only after payment (unlock_transaction_id).

FR-38.3 Institute routing. Institute leads go to the manager; the manager may assign an institute teacher (assigned_institute_teacher_id). Response time counts from creation to first manager/teacher action.

FR-38.4 Metrics (computed, not stored). Response rate = leads with first_response_at within 24 h ÷ non-spam leads in the window; median first response time; conversion rate = converted ÷ non-spam leads. Available per teacher/institute/city in GET /leads/stats.

FR-38.5 Detail timeline. Built from lead columns, the related demo_requests row, related complaints, and audit log entries for the lead (admin changes).

FR-38.6 Admin notes. admin_note is internal, never shown in the app; each change is audited with the previous text.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
status (PATCH) one of viewed, contacted, converted, declined, closed, spam; not new
reason required 10–300 chars when setting spam, declined or closed by admin
adminNote ≤ 1,000 chars
query dates from ≤ to, range ≤ 366 days
If-Match required on PATCH

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /leads leads.read List with filters
GET /leads/stats leads.read Funnel and response metrics for the current filters
GET /leads/:id leads.read Detail with timeline
PATCH /leads/:id/status leads.manage Correct status (If-Match)
POST /leads/:id/spam leads.manage Mark as spam
POST /leads/:id/not-spam leads.manage Undo spam within 7 days
PATCH /leads/:id/note leads.manage Set internal note

9. PostgreSQL Tables

leads

Enquiries and call-back requests from parents/students to a teacher or institute.

CREATE TABLE leads (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  public_code text NOT NULL DEFAULT ('LD-' || nextval('seq_lead_code')), -- e.g. LD-240981
  lead_type text NOT NULL CHECK (lead_type IN ('inquiry','callback','demo')), -- demo leads also have a demo_requests row
  target_type text NOT NULL CHECK (target_type IN ('teacher','institute')), -- Who receives it
  teacher_id uuid REFERENCES teachers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Target teacher
  institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Target institute
  requester_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Who asked
  requester_type text NOT NULL CHECK (requester_type IN ('parent','student')), -- Requester role
  child_id uuid REFERENCES parent_children(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Child the request is for
  subject_id uuid REFERENCES subjects(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Subject asked about
  class_id uuid REFERENCES classes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Class
  message text, -- Requester message, max 1,000 chars
  preferred_callback_window text, -- e.g. Today 6–8 PM
  source text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'profile' CHECK (source IN ('profile','search','recommendation','featured','compare','institute_page','other')), -- Where it started
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new' CHECK (status IN ('new','viewed','contacted','converted','declined','closed','spam')), -- Lifecycle
  contact_unlocked boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Requester phone shared with the teacher
  unlock_transaction_id uuid, -- Paid contact unlock (FK added in migration 040)
  assigned_institute_teacher_id uuid REFERENCES institute_teachers(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Institute leads: teacher the manager assigned
  first_response_at timestamptz, -- First reply or status change by the receiver (response-rate metric)
  closed_at timestamptz, -- When closed/converted/declined
  decline_reason text, -- Reason given by the teacher
  admin_note text, -- Internal note from support
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  deleted_at timestamptz, -- Soft delete
  CONSTRAINT ck_leads_target CHECK ((target_type = 'teacher' AND teacher_id IS NOT NULL AND institute_id IS NULL) OR (target_type = 'institute' AND institute_id IS NOT NULL AND teacher_id IS NULL))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_leads_public_code ON leads (public_code);
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_teacher ON leads (teacher_id, status, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_institute ON leads (institute_id, status, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_requester ON leads (requester_user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_leads_status_created ON leads (status, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_leads_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON leads FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();
ALTER TABLE leads ADD CONSTRAINT fk_leads_unlock_txn FOREIGN KEY (unlock_transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

Module 39 · Demo Class Requests

Phase 11 · Leads · Depends on: M38 · Owns tables: demo_requests · Reads: leads, teachers, institutes, app_users, parent_children, teaching_modes · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Overview

Free demo classes booked by parents or students with a teacher (or campus visits with an institute). Every demo has a parent lead of type demo. Admins see all demos, their schedule and outcome, can cancel or reschedule on behalf of users when support is asked, and track no-shows that feed teacher analytics and requester strikes.

2. Business Purpose

Demos are the strongest conversion step. Support must be able to fix a demo when one side can't use the app, and operations needs no-show and completion rates to protect families' time and teachers' reputations.

3. User Stories

  • As Support Admin, I want to reschedule a demo for a parent who called in so that the booking isn't lost.
  • As Operations Admin, I want the no-show rate per teacher so that I can act on unreliable teachers.
  • As Operations Admin, I want the demo → enrolment rate by subject so that marketing knows what converts.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-39.1 Lifecycle.

From To Actor Rule
— requested requester slot ≥ 2 h and ≤ 21 days ahead; max 3 open demos per requester
requested confirmed teacher / institute sets confirmed_start_at; meeting link required for online mode
requested / confirmed reschedule_proposed either side / admin new slot stored as confirmed_start_at proposal; other side accepts → confirmed
requested expired system not confirmed 1 h before requested_start_at
confirmed completed either side after start + duration, or admin sets completed_at; prompts outcome and review
confirmed no_show either side within 24 h after start, or admin no-show attributed via cancelled_by = the side that didn't attend
any open cancelled either side / admin cancelled_by, cancel_reason required

FR-39.2 Lead sync. Demo completed with outcome enrolled sets the lead to converted; cancelled / expired leave the lead open for follow-up.

FR-39.3 Reminders. Job sends a push 1 h before confirmed_start_at (sets reminder_sent_at) to both sides.

FR-39.4 Admin actions. Cancel (reason, notify both sides), reschedule (new slot, notify both; goes to confirmed directly when the admin confirms both sides agreed by phone — confirmedByPhone: true required), mark completed / no-show (who did not attend).

FR-39.5 Clash check. Confirming or rescheduling rejects a slot overlapping another confirmed demo of the same teacher (idx_demo_requests_teacher_time).

FR-39.6 Metrics. Completion rate, no-show rate (split teacher vs requester), average lead-to-demo time, demo → enrolment rate. Available via GET /demos/stats.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
startAt ISO datetime, ≥ now + 1 h, ≤ now + 21 days
durationMinutes 15–120
meetingLink https URL, required when teaching mode is online
reason 10–300 chars for cancel, no-show, admin reschedule
noShowParty teacher or requester
confirmedByPhone must be true for admin reschedule straight to confirmed

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /demos demos.read List with filters
GET /demos/stats demos.read Completion, no-show and conversion metrics
GET /demos/calendar demos.read Demos in a date window for the calendar view
GET /demos/:id demos.read Detail
POST /demos/:id/cancel demos.manage Cancel on behalf of a user
POST /demos/:id/reschedule demos.manage Propose or confirm a new slot
POST /demos/:id/complete demos.manage Mark completed with outcome
POST /demos/:id/no-show demos.manage Mark no-show

demo_requests

Free demo class bookings and their outcome.

CREATE TABLE demo_requests (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  lead_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Parent lead (lead_type = demo)
  teacher_id uuid REFERENCES teachers(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Teacher giving the demo
  institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Institute giving the demo / campus visit
  requester_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Learner or parent
  child_id uuid REFERENCES parent_children(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Child attending
  teaching_mode_id uuid REFERENCES teaching_modes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Online / home / at teacher's place
  requested_start_at timestamptz NOT NULL, -- Slot the requester picked
  confirmed_start_at timestamptz, -- Slot the teacher confirmed
  duration_minutes smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 45 CHECK (duration_minutes BETWEEN 15 AND 120), -- Length
  meeting_link text, -- Online class link (https)
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requested' CHECK (status IN ('requested','confirmed','reschedule_proposed','completed','cancelled','no_show','expired')), -- Lifecycle
  cancelled_by text CHECK (cancelled_by IN ('requester','teacher','institute','admin','system')), -- Who cancelled
  cancel_reason text, -- Why cancelled
  outcome text CHECK (outcome IN ('enrolled','not_enrolled','undecided')), -- Result reported after the demo
  reminder_sent_at timestamptz, -- 1-hour reminder push sent
  completed_at timestamptz, -- Marked completed
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  CONSTRAINT ck_demo_requests_target CHECK (teacher_id IS NOT NULL OR institute_id IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_demo_requests_lead ON demo_requests (lead_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_demo_requests_teacher_time ON demo_requests (teacher_id, confirmed_start_at) WHERE status IN ('requested','confirmed','reschedule_proposed');
CREATE INDEX idx_demo_requests_status ON demo_requests (status, requested_start_at);

demo.completed_by_admin outcome
demo.no_show_marked party, reason

Teacher availability calendars with bookable slots; in-app video classes; paid trial classes (new fee code); Google/Outlook calendar sync.

Module 40 · Transactions

Phase 12 · Payments · Depends on: M5, M16, M22 (M41 creates subscription payments) · Owns tables: transactions, refunds, payment_webhook_events · Reads: app_users, institutes, payment_configurations, teachers, leads, subscriptions · Build estimate: 5 days

1. Module Overview

The payments ledger. Every Razorpay payment attempt (registrations, subscriptions, premium/featured listings, contact unlocks), every refund and every referral payout is a row in transactions. Webhooks are stored raw in payment_webhook_events and processed exactly once. Admins can search and inspect transactions, reconcile with Razorpay, download GST invoices, and request/approve/deny refunds.

2. Business Purpose

Money must be correct to the paisa and explainable. Finance needs reconciliation and invoices; support needs to answer "I paid but nothing happened"; the business needs refunds to be controlled (maker-checker) and traceable.

3. User Stories

  • As Finance Admin, I want to find a payment by Razorpay payment id so that I can reconcile a bank statement line.
  • As Support Admin, I want to request a refund for a teacher whose registration was rejected so that finance can approve it.
  • As Finance Admin, I want to approve refunds created by support, but not my own, so that no one person can move money alone.
  • As Support Admin, I want to re-sync a payment stuck in created so that a user who paid gets access.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-40.1 Payment flow (mobile API, documented for admins).

  1. App calls POST /app/v1/payments/orders { feeCode, context }. Server reads the active payment configuration for the fee code (Module 5), rejects if disabled, computes base_amount_paise, GST 18 % (gst_paise = round(base × 0.18)), discounts (referral), creates the Razorpay order with receipt = public_code, inserts transactions (created, payment_configuration_id, fee_code snapshot).
  2. App completes Checkout; server verifies the signature HMAC_SHA256(order_id|payment_id, key_secret) and marks authorized/captured.
  3. Webhook payment.captured is the source of truth: store in payment_webhook_events (ON CONFLICT (gateway, event_id) DO NOTHING), verify X-Razorpay-Signature, process in a BullMQ job: set captured, captured_at, method, invoice number (GC/<FY>/<6-digit sequence per FY>, from sequence seq_invoice_<fy> e.g. seq_invoice_2026_27, created on first use with CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS; gaps are allowed by GST rules only if cancelled numbers are recorded, so numbers are assigned only on capture), then fulfil by purpose (activate subscription, mark registration paid, start premium/featured window, unlock lead). Fulfilment is idempotent (checks current state first).
  4. payment.failed sets failed with failure_code/failure_reason. Orders not captured within 30 min → cancelled by job.

FR-40.2 Refunds (maker-checker).

  • Created by admin (POST /transactions/:id/refunds), by the system (e.g. teacher rejected within 7 days of paying → auto request teacher_rejected), or by the user via support.
  • Amount ≤ amount_paise − refunded_amount_paise − pending refund amounts.
  • Approval by an admin with refunds.approve who is not the requester; approval calls Razorpay POST /payments/:id/refund with Idempotency-Key = refund.id; status processing; webhook refund.processed → processed, updates refunded_amount_paise and transaction status (refunded if fully, else partially_refunded). refund.failed → failed (can be retried).
  • Side effects on full refund: subscription → cancelled (reason refunded), premium/featured window ended, registration remains but registration_paid cleared.
  • Deny requires denialReason shown to the user.

FR-40.3 Reconciliation. POST /transactions/:id/sync fetches the payment from Razorpay and applies any missed state (idempotent). Nightly job compares the day's Razorpay settlements report with captured transactions and lists mismatches (GET /transactions/reconciliation?date=).

FR-40.4 Webhook console. GET /payment-webhooks lists events with processing state; POST /payment-webhooks/:id/retry re-queues a failed event. Events with signature_valid = false are never processed.

FR-40.5 Invoices. GET /transactions/:id/invoice returns a presigned URL to a PDF generated on capture (GSTIN, HSN/SAC 999293, place of supply from user state). Credit notes are generated for processed refunds.

FR-40.6 Manual transactions. Offline payments (bank transfer from institutes) can be recorded with gateway = manual, method = manual, a reference and a proof file; requires refunds.approve (finance) and a second admin's confirmation before fulfilment.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
refund.amountPaise integer > 0, ≤ refundable amount
refund.reasonCode one of the table's reason codes
refund.reasonNote 10–500 chars; required for goodwill and other
deny.denialReason 10–300 chars
manual.referenceNumber 6–40 chars, unique per manual transaction
query amountMin/amountMax integers in paise, min ≤ max
Idempotency-Key required on refund create and manual transaction create

9. PostgreSQL Tables

transactions

Every payment attempt through Razorpay, plus refunds and reward payouts. Amounts in paise.

CREATE TABLE transactions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  public_code text NOT NULL DEFAULT ('TXN-' || nextval('seq_transaction_code')), -- e.g. TXN-7702137 (shown to users and support)
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Payer or payee
  payer_type text NOT NULL CHECK (payer_type IN ('parent','student','teacher','institute')), -- Payer role
  institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Set for institute payments
  purpose text NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('teacher_registration','institute_registration','subscription','premium_listing','featured_listing','contact_unlock','referral_payout')), -- What was bought / paid out
  direction text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'credit' CHECK (direction IN ('credit','debit')), -- credit = money in to GuruConnect; debit = payout
  payment_configuration_id uuid REFERENCES payment_configurations(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Price version charged (NULL for payouts)
  fee_code text, -- Snapshot of fee_code
  amount_paise bigint NOT NULL CHECK (amount_paise >= 0), -- Total charged incl. GST
  base_amount_paise bigint NOT NULL CHECK (base_amount_paise >= 0), -- Amount before GST
  gst_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (gst_paise >= 0), -- GST component
  discount_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (discount_paise >= 0), -- Referral / promo discount applied
  currency char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INR', -- Currency
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'created' CHECK (status IN ('created','authorized','captured','failed','refund_pending','refunded','partially_refunded','cancelled')), -- Lifecycle
  gateway text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'razorpay' CHECK (gateway IN ('razorpay','manual','wallet')), -- Processor
  gateway_order_id text, -- Razorpay order_xxx
  gateway_payment_id text, -- Razorpay pay_xxx
  method text CHECK (method IN ('upi','card','netbanking','wallet','emi','manual')), -- Payment method
  failure_code text, -- Gateway error code
  failure_reason text, -- Gateway error description
  refunded_amount_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (refunded_amount_paise >= 0), -- Total refunded
  invoice_number text, -- GST invoice number, e.g. GC/2026-27/000412
  captured_at timestamptz, -- When money was captured
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb, -- Extra context, e.g. {"subscription_id":"…","lead_id":"…"}
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  CONSTRAINT ck_transactions_refund CHECK (refunded_amount_paise <= amount_paise)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_transactions_public_code ON transactions (public_code);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_transactions_gateway_order ON transactions (gateway_order_id) WHERE gateway_order_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_transactions_gateway_payment ON transactions (gateway_payment_id) WHERE gateway_payment_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_transactions_invoice ON transactions (invoice_number) WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_user ON transactions (user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_status_created ON transactions (status, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_transactions_purpose_captured ON transactions (purpose, captured_at) WHERE status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded');
CREATE TRIGGER trg_transactions_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON transactions FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

refunds

Refund requests and their gateway processing.

CREATE TABLE refunds (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  transaction_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Original payment
  amount_paise bigint NOT NULL CHECK (amount_paise > 0), -- Amount to refund
  reason_code text NOT NULL CHECK (reason_code IN ('teacher_rejected','institute_rejected','duplicate_charge','service_not_started','user_request','goodwill','other')), -- Why
  reason_note text, -- Details
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requested' CHECK (status IN ('requested','approved','processing','processed','denied','failed')), -- Lifecycle
  gateway_refund_id text, -- Razorpay rfnd_xxx
  requested_by_type text NOT NULL CHECK (requested_by_type IN ('app_user','admin','system')), -- Who asked
  requested_by_id uuid, -- Requester id
  decided_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Approver / denier
  decided_at timestamptz, -- Decision time
  denial_reason text, -- Shown to the user
  processed_at timestamptz, -- Gateway confirmed
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Updated
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_refunds_gateway ON refunds (gateway_refund_id) WHERE gateway_refund_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_refunds_status ON refunds (status, created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_refunds_transaction ON refunds (transaction_id);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_refunds_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON refunds FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

payment_webhook_events

Raw Razorpay webhooks, stored before processing so every event is processed exactly once.

CREATE TABLE payment_webhook_events (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  gateway text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'razorpay', -- Source
  event_id text NOT NULL, -- Gateway event id (x-razorpay-event-id)
  event_type text NOT NULL, -- e.g. payment.captured, refund.processed
  payload jsonb NOT NULL, -- Full body
  signature_valid boolean NOT NULL, -- HMAC check result
  processed_at timestamptz, -- NULL until processed
  processing_error text, -- Last error
  attempts smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Processing attempts
  received_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Received
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_payment_webhook_events ON payment_webhook_events (gateway, event_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_payment_webhook_unprocessed ON payment_webhook_events (received_at) WHERE processed_at IS NULL;

Migration file: sql/migrations/040_m40_transactions.sql

12. Indexing Strategy

Index Table Kind Definition
uq_transactions_public_code transactions unique (public_code)
uq_transactions_gateway_order transactions unique (gateway_order_id) WHERE gateway_order_id IS NOT NULL
uq_transactions_gateway_payment transactions unique (gateway_payment_id) WHERE gateway_payment_id IS NOT NULL
uq_transactions_invoice transactions unique (invoice_number) WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL
idx_transactions_user transactions btree (user_id, created_at DESC)
idx_transactions_status_created transactions btree (status, created_at DESC)
idx_transactions_purpose_captured transactions btree (purpose, captured_at) WHERE status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded')
uq_refunds_gateway refunds unique (gateway_refund_id) WHERE gateway_refund_id IS NOT NULL
idx_refunds_status refunds btree (status, created_at)
idx_refunds_transaction refunds btree (transaction_id)
uq_payment_webhook_events payment_webhook_events unique (gateway, event_id)
idx_payment_webhook_unprocessed payment_webhook_events btree (received_at) WHERE processed_at IS NULL

Unique partial indexes on gateway_order_id, gateway_payment_id, invoice_number make webhook processing idempotent and lookups O(log n). idx_transactions_purpose_captured serves revenue reports; idx_transactions_status_created the list; idx_payment_webhook_unprocessed the retry job; uq_payment_webhook_events (gateway, event_id) deduplicates deliveries.

Scenario HTTP Code Message

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

Wallet balances for referral credits (wallets, wallet_entries double-entry ledger); multiple gateways (PhonePe/Cashfree) behind a PaymentGateway interface; partitioning transactions by financial year; automated settlement ingestion via Razorpay Settlements API; GST e-invoicing (IRN) when turnover requires it.

22. Security Considerations

Razorpay key secret and webhook secret in the secrets manager, never in the DB. Webhook route uses the raw body for HMAC and constant-time comparison. Card data never touches our servers (Checkout). refunds.approve is sensitive and requires a fresh re-auth (≤ 5 min) on approve. Payer PII masked without users.pii.

Module 41 · Subscription Payments

Phase 12 · Payments · Depends on: M5, M40 (used by M30, M32 and teacher/institute registration) · Owns tables: subscriptions · Reads: app_users, institutes, payment_configurations, transactions, admins · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

Paid access periods: parent and student memberships (monthly/yearly with trials), teacher and institute annual registrations, and admin-granted complimentary or free-access periods when a fee is switched off. This module owns the subscription state machine, renewal and expiry jobs, and the admin tools to grant, extend and cancel. Modules 30 and 32 are the parent- and student-facing admin views over the same table.

2. Business Purpose

Subscription state decides what every user can do in the app, so it must be unambiguous (one live subscription per user and type), priced from the price version in force at purchase, and adjustable by admins with a reason when support needs to make things right.

3. User Stories

  • As Finance Admin, I want to see all live subscriptions by plan so that I can forecast renewals.
  • As Support Admin, I want to extend a parent's membership by 7 days after an outage so that they aren't charged for downtime.
  • As Super Admin, I want users to keep access when I switch a fee off, and to move them to a trial when I switch it back on.
  • As Finance Admin, I want failed renewals to enter a grace period so that users have time to fix payment.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-41.1 States.

Status Meaning Access
trial Free trial (trial_days of the fee config) Full
active Paid period Full
grace Renewal failed; 3 days to pay Full, banner in app
expired Period over None
cancelled Cancelled by user/admin/system (refund) Until ends_at for user cancels; immediate for admin/refund
free_access Fee disabled by admin Full, no end date

Only one row per (user, subscriber_type) may be in trial/active/grace/free_access (uq_subscriptions_one_live). Renewing creates a new row after the previous ends, preserving history.

FR-41.2 Purchase. On capture (Module 40) for a subscription fee code: if a live trial exists, end it and start active now; if a live active exists, the new period starts at its ends_at (queued row stored with status active only when it begins — the job activates it; until then the payment's metadata holds the pending period). price_paise = amount paid (base), payment_configuration_id = version charged. Period length = validity_days of that version.

FR-41.3 Auto-renew. If auto_renew (Razorpay subscription / UPI Autopay mandate), the charge on ends_at creates the next period; failure → grace for 3 days, then expired. Price changes (Module 5) apply at next renewal; users are notified 7 days before (renewal_reminder_sent_at) with the new price.

FR-41.4 Jobs (hourly). trial → expired (or → active if a payment exists), active → expired at ends_at when not auto-renewing, grace → expired after 3 days, 7-day renewal reminders.

FR-41.5 Fee switched off / on (Module 5 hook). Disabling a fee code: all users of that type without a live row get free_access rows; existing active rows continue. Enabling: free_access rows are ended (cancelled, cancelled_by_type = system); if setting subscriptions.free_access_to_trial_on_enable is true they receive a trial of the fee's trial_days, otherwise access ends with a 3-day notice.

FR-41.6 Admin actions.

  • Grant complimentary: creates active with price_paise = 0, granted_by, ends_at ≤ 365 days; fails if a live row exists (use extend).
  • Extend: moves ends_at of the live row by 1–90 days.
  • Cancel: immediate (access ends now) or at period end; optional refund request (creates a Module 40 refund, maker-checker still applies).
  • Change auto-renew: turn off only (turning on requires the user's mandate). All actions require a reason and send the user a notification.

FR-41.7 Metrics. Active by plan, trials, trial → paid conversion, churn (expired without renewal ÷ due), MRR (monthly-equivalent of active paid rows: yearly price ÷ 12), renewals due next 7/30 days.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
grant.subscriberType parent, student, teacher, institute; must match the user's role
grant.feeCode a fee code valid for that subscriber type
grant.endsAt > now, ≤ now + 365 days
extend.days integer 1–90
cancel.mode immediate or period_end
cancel.refundAmountPaise optional, ≤ refundable amount of last_transaction_id
reason 10–300 chars on every action
If-Match required on extend / cancel

subscriptions

CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Subscriber account

Module 42 · Referral Management

Phase 13 · Referrals · Depends on: M6, M40 · Owns tables: referral_codes, referrals · Reads: app_users, referral_settings, transactions, admins · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

Tracks every referral from code to reward: personal referral codes (one per user per program), admin campaign codes, referrals created at sign-up, qualification on the program's qualifying event, fraud scoring, the reward hold period and payout as wallet credit. Admins review held (suspicious) referrals, reverse fraudulent rewards and manage campaign codes. Program rules are configured in Module 6.

2. Business Purpose

Referrals are the cheapest acquisition channel in India's word-of-mouth tutoring market, and also the easiest to abuse. The module has to pay genuine referrers quickly and stop self-referral and fake-number farms.

3. User Stories

  • As Operations Admin, I want to see the top referrers this month so that we can thank them.
  • As Finance Admin, I want held referrals with fraud flags so that I can release or reject each with a reason.
  • As Marketing (Operations Admin), I want a campaign code "SCHOOLFAIR26" limited to 500 sign-ups so that I can measure an event.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-42.1 Codes. Every app user gets a personal code on first need (<FIRSTNAME><2–3 digits>, upper-case, unique case-insensitively). Campaign codes are created by admins with optional usage limit and expiry; user_id NULL.

FR-42.2 Attribution. At sign-up the app sends the code; the server creates a referrals row (pending) with the active referral_settings version of the program at that moment. A user can be referred only once (uq_referrals_referee); self-referral (same phone/device) is rejected.

FR-42.3 Qualification. On the program's qualifying event (first_payment → first captured transaction; teacher_approved; institute_approved), the referral becomes qualified with qualified_at, reward_release_at = qualified_at + reward_hold_days, amounts copied from the settings version. If the referrer has reached max_rewards_per_month, status stays qualified with reason monthly_cap and rewards 0.

FR-42.4 Fraud scoring (at sign-up and qualification). Score 0–1 from flags: same_device (0.6), same_ip_24h ≥ 3 (0.3), burst_signups (≥ 5 referees in 1 h, 0.3), disposable_number (0.4), referee_inactive (no session after qualification, 0.2); capped at 1. Score ≥ 0.5 → on_hold for admin review.

FR-42.5 Payout. Job at reward_release_at: for qualified rows not refunded/reversed, create transactions with purpose = referral_payout, direction = debit, gateway = wallet, then rewarded. If the qualifying payment is fully refunded before release → expired. Referee reward (discount) is applied at checkout (Module 40 discount_paise), not paid out.

FR-42.6 Admin review. Release (held → qualified, payout on schedule or immediately with releaseNow), reject (with reason, no reward), reverse (after reward: reverses wallet credit via a counter transaction; if wallet balance is insufficient, the balance goes negative and future credits settle it).

FR-42.7 Stats. Sign-ups via referral, qualified %, rewards paid, cost per acquisition (rewards ÷ qualified), top referrers, fraud rate; per program and campaign code.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
code (campaign) 4–20 chars, ^[A-Z0-9]+$, unique case-insensitive
campaignName 3–80 chars
usageLimit integer 1–1,000,000 or null
expiresAt > now
programCode LEARNER_REFERRAL, TEACHER_REFERRAL, INSTITUTE_REFERRAL
reason 10–300 chars on release/reject/reverse/disable

9. PostgreSQL Tables

referral_codes

One personal referral code per app user.

CREATE TABLE referral_codes (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  user_id uuid REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Owner; NULL for admin campaign codes
  code text NOT NULL, -- Upper-case code, e.g. LAKSHMI50
  program_code text NOT NULL CHECK (program_code IN ('LEARNER_REFERRAL','TEACHER_REFERRAL','INSTITUTE_REFERRAL')), -- Program
  campaign_name text, -- For admin-created campaign codes
  usage_limit integer CHECK (usage_limit IS NULL OR usage_limit > 0), -- Max sign-ups (campaign codes)
  expires_at timestamptz, -- Campaign expiry
  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Disabled codes stop working
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin creator (campaign codes)
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Created
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_referral_codes_code ON referral_codes (upper(code));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_referral_codes_user_program ON referral_codes (user_id, program_code) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL;

referrals

One row per referred user, tracking qualification, fraud checks and reward payout.

CREATE TABLE referrals (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  referral_code_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES referral_codes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Code used
  referrer_user_id uuid REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Who invited (NULL for campaign codes)
  referee_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Who joined
  referral_setting_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES referral_settings(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Rules version applied
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','qualified','on_hold','rewarded','rejected','expired','reversed')), -- Lifecycle
  qualified_at timestamptz, -- Qualifying event time
  qualifying_transaction_id uuid REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Payment that qualified it
  reward_amount_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reward_amount_paise >= 0), -- Referrer reward
  referee_reward_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (referee_reward_paise >= 0), -- Referee reward/discount
  reward_release_at timestamptz, -- End of hold period
  reward_transaction_id uuid REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Payout record
  fraud_score numeric(4,3) CHECK (fraud_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1), -- Automated risk score
  fraud_flags text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- e.g. {same_device, burst_signups, disposable_number}
  reviewed_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Admin who reviewed a held referral
  reviewed_at timestamptz, -- Review time
  rejection_reason text, -- Why rejected / reversed
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created (referee signed up)
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Updated
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_referrals_referee ON referrals (referee_user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_referrals_referrer ON referrals (referrer_user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_referrals_status ON referrals (status, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_referrals_release ON referrals (reward_release_at) WHERE status = 'qualified';
CREATE TRIGGER trg_referrals_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON referrals FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

Scenario HTTP Code Message
Code already exists 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE "That code is already in use."
Release a non-held referral 409 CONFLICT_STATE "Only referrals on hold can be released."
Reverse before reward 409 CONFLICT_STATE "Nothing to reverse yet — reject instead."
Usage limit below current uses 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "This code has already been used {n} times."

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

Tiered rewards (more after 5 referrals); cash payouts to bank via RazorpayX (KYC needed); device fingerprint service; share-link attribution with deep links.

22. Security Considerations

Fraud signals (device ids, IPs) are visible only to referrals.review; reversal of paid rewards is sensitive and fully audited.

Module 43 · Complaint Management

Phase 14 · Complaints · Depends on: M0, M16, M22, M28, M31, M38 (feeds M36 complaints factor) · Owns tables: complaints, complaint_actions, complaint_attachments · Reads: app_users, institutes, leads, admins, files, teachers, trust_scores · Build estimate: 5 days

1. Module Overview

Two-way safety reporting. Parents and students can report teachers and institutes; teachers can report parents and students. Each report becomes a case with a number, severity, SLA, owner and timeline. Admins triage, request information, add evidence, issue warnings, suspend accounts, escalate, and resolve or dismiss with a message to the reporter. Upheld complaints lower the teacher's trust score (Module 36).

2. Business Purpose

Families invite teachers into their homes and children meet them alone; teachers enter strangers' homes. Fast, fair handling of reports is the platform's most important safety obligation and a legal one (IT Rules 2021 grievance timelines: acknowledge within 24 h, resolve within 15 days).

3. User Stories

  • As Support Admin, I want critical cases (harassment, safety) at the top with an SLA countdown so that nothing urgent waits.
  • As Support Admin, I want to suspend a teacher from inside the case so that the action and the reason stay linked.
  • As Super Admin, I want to see every past complaint about the same person so that I can recognise patterns.
  • As Support Admin, I want to ask the reporter for more information and pause the SLA until they reply.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-43.1 Intake (mobile API). Reporter picks the person/institute (from a lead, profile or chat), type, description (20–3,000 chars) and up to 5 attachments (images/PDF ≤ 10 MB, private). case_number = CS- + sequence. An auto-acknowledgement push/email is sent immediately.

FR-43.2 Triage rules (on create).

Condition Severity
type harassment, or description matches safety keywords (list in settings complaints.safety_keywords), or reported party has ≥ 2 complaints in 30 days critical
type fraud high
misconduct medium
fake_information, other low
sla_due_at = created + 4 h (critical), 24 h (high), 72 h (medium/low). Critical cases page on-call support (email + push to admins with complaints.manage subscribed to alerts) and, for reported teachers, auto-freeze the trust score (Module 36) until resolved.

FR-43.3 Lifecycle.

From To Action
open in_review assign (self or other)
in_review awaiting_info request info from reporter or reported (message sent; SLA paused, stored in metadata)
awaiting_info in_review reply received or 7 days pass
open / in_review escalated escalate to Super Admin (required for bans and police referral)
any open resolved with resolution, is_upheld, resolution_note, reporter_message
any open dismissed not upheld; reason + reporter message
resolved / dismissed in_review reopen within 30 days with reason

FR-43.4 Enforcement (complaints.enforce).

  • Warning: notification to the reported user with template text; logged as warning_issued; 3 warnings in 12 months suggests suspension.
  • Suspend: calls the same suspend service as Modules 17 / 24 / 28 / 31 (account_status = 'suspended' on the role row and app_users; teachers: hidden from search, leads blocked; institutes: hidden; parents/students: cannot create leads) for 7/30/90 days or until lifted; stored in complaint_actions.metadata {"days":30,"until":"…"}; job lifts it.
  • Ban (account_banned resolution): only from escalated by Super Admin; permanent; sets app_users.account_status = 'banned' (sign-in blocked, sessions revoked) and the role row to suspended with no end date.
  • Refund issued: links a Module 40 refund. Each enforcement is a separate audited action and notification.

FR-43.5 Trust effect. On resolve/dismiss/reopen of a complaint against a teacher, enqueue trust recalculation (complaint_resolved); is_upheld = true counts in the complaints factor for 12 months.

FR-43.6 History. GET /complaints/:id includes other complaints involving the same reported party and the same reporter (to spot serial reporters).

FR-43.7 SLA. sla_breached = now > sla_due_at AND status IN (open, in_review, escalated); breaches listed on the dashboard; hourly job notifies assignees 1 h before breach.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
assign.adminId active admin with complaints.manage
severity low, medium, high, critical; change needs reason
note 2–3,000 chars; isInternal boolean (default true)
requestInfo.to reporter or reported; message 20–1,000 chars
resolve.resolution one of the table values; account_banned only from escalated by Super Admin
resolve.isUpheld required boolean
resolve.reporterMessage 20–1,000 chars
suspend.days 7, 30, 90 or null (until lifted)
attachments ≤ 5 per upload call, image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf, ≤ 10 MB
If-Match required on state changes

9. PostgreSQL Tables

complaints

Two-way safety reports: learners about teachers/institutes, teachers about parents/students.

CREATE TABLE complaints (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  case_number text NOT NULL DEFAULT ('CS-' || nextval('seq_case_number')), -- e.g. CS-4471
  reporter_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Who reported
  reporter_type text NOT NULL CHECK (reporter_type IN ('parent','student','teacher','institute_staff')), -- Reporter role
  reported_type text NOT NULL CHECK (reported_type IN ('teacher','institute','parent','student')), -- Who is reported
  reported_user_id uuid REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Reported account (teacher/parent/student)
  reported_institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Reported institute
  lead_id uuid REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Related lead, if any
  complaint_type text NOT NULL CHECK (complaint_type IN ('fraud','misconduct','fake_information','harassment','other')), -- Type
  description text NOT NULL, -- What happened, 20–3,000 chars
  severity text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium' CHECK (severity IN ('low','medium','high','critical')), -- Set by triage rules, editable by admin
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open','in_review','awaiting_info','escalated','resolved','dismissed')), -- Lifecycle
  assigned_admin_id uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Case owner
  resolution text CHECK (resolution IN ('no_action','warning_issued','content_removed','account_suspended','account_banned','refund_issued','referred_to_police')), -- Outcome
  resolution_note text, -- Explanation (internal)
  reporter_message text, -- Message sent to the reporter on closure
  is_upheld boolean, -- true when the complaint was valid; feeds the trust score
  sla_due_at timestamptz NOT NULL, -- Response due (critical 4h, high 24h, else 72h)
  resolved_at timestamptz, -- Closed
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  CONSTRAINT ck_complaints_target CHECK ((reported_type = 'institute') = (reported_institute_id IS NOT NULL) AND (reported_type = 'institute' OR reported_user_id IS NOT NULL))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_complaints_case ON complaints (case_number);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaints_queue ON complaints (status, severity, sla_due_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaints_reported_user ON complaints (reported_user_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaints_reported_inst ON complaints (reported_institute_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaints_assignee ON complaints (assigned_admin_id, status);
CREATE TRIGGER trg_complaints_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON complaints FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

complaint_actions

Case timeline: assignments, notes, warnings, suspensions, escalations.

CREATE TABLE complaint_actions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  complaint_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES complaints(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Case
  action text NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('created','assigned','note','info_requested','warning_issued','suspended','escalated','severity_changed','resolved','dismissed','reopened')), -- Event
  note text, -- Details
  is_internal boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- false = shown to reporter/reported
  metadata jsonb, -- e.g. {"from":"medium","to":"high"}
  admin_id uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Actor
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- When
);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaint_actions_case ON complaint_actions (complaint_id, created_at);

complaint_attachments

Evidence files attached to a complaint.

CREATE TABLE complaint_attachments (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  complaint_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES complaints(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Case
  file_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Private file
  uploaded_by_type text NOT NULL CHECK (uploaded_by_type IN ('app_user','admin')), -- Uploader kind
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Uploaded
);
CREATE INDEX idx_complaint_attachments_case ON complaint_attachments (complaint_id);

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

Module 44 · Banner Management

Phase 15 · CMS · Depends on: M0, M9 · Owns tables: banners · Reads: files, cities, admins · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Overview

Promotional banners shown in the mobile app at fixed placements (home top carousel, home middle, inline in search, teacher and institute dashboards, onboarding). Admins create banners with an image, title, deep link, audience, cities and a schedule; banners go live and expire automatically, can be paused, and report impressions and clicks.

2. Business Purpose

Lets marketing and operations run campaigns (exam season, referral pushes, teacher recruitment) without an app release, targeted to the right audience and city.

3. User Stories

  • As Operations Admin, I want to schedule a "Board exam crash courses" banner for Class 10/12 parents in Bengaluru from 1–31 Jan so that it runs without me.
  • As Operations Admin, I want to see click-through rate per banner so that I can keep what works.
  • As Operations Admin, I want to reorder banners in a placement so that the most important shows first.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-44.1 Lifecycle. draft → (publish) → scheduled if starts_at > now else active; active ⇄ paused; job every 5 minutes: scheduled → active at starts_at, active → expired at ends_at. Deleting is soft and only for non-active banners.

FR-44.2 Serving (mobile API). GET /app/v1/banners?placement= returns active banners matching the user's audience and city (empty city_ids = all), ordered by priority desc then starts_at desc, max 5 per placement; cached in Redis 5 min per (placement, audience, city) and invalidated on any banner change.

FR-44.3 Metrics. The app batches impression and click events (POST /app/v1/events); a job aggregates them every 15 minutes into impressions/clicks. CTR = clicks ÷ impressions.

FR-44.4 Image. Uploaded through Module 0 (public bucket), 1080×480 (2.25:1), JPEG/PNG/WebP, ≤ 500 KB; server validates dimensions.

FR-44.5 Deep links. Allowed: app routes from a registry (gc://search?subjectId=…, gc://plans, gc://referral, gc://blog/<slug>, gc://teacher/<id>) or https:// URLs on an allow-listed domain (settings banners.allowed_domains).

FR-44.6 Reorder. POST /banners/reorder { placement, ids[] } sets priority descending in the given order.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
title 3–60 chars
subtitle ≤ 90 chars
imageFileId uploaded, public, image, 1080×480 ± 2 px
placement one of the six placements
audience all, parents, students, teachers, institutes
cityIds array of active city ids, ≤ 50
deepLink registry route or allow-listed https URL
startsAt / endsAt endsAt > startsAt; endsAt ≤ startsAt + 180 days
priority 0–100

6. API Endpoints

Method Path Permission Description
GET /banners banners.read List with filters and CTR
GET /banners/:id banners.read Detail
POST /banners banners.manage Create (draft)
PATCH /banners/:id banners.manage Edit (If-Match)
POST /banners/:id/publish banners.manage Publish (scheduled or active)
POST /banners/:id/pause banners.manage Pause
POST /banners/:id/resume banners.manage Resume
POST /banners/reorder banners.manage Set order within a placement
DELETE /banners/:id banners.manage Soft delete (not active)
GET /banners/preview banners.read What a given audience/city sees per placement

9. PostgreSQL Tables

banners

Promotional banners in the mobile app.

CREATE TABLE banners (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  title text NOT NULL, -- Headline, max 60 chars
  subtitle text, -- Supporting line, max 90 chars
  image_file_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- 1080×480 image (public)
  placement text NOT NULL CHECK (placement IN ('home_top','home_middle','search_inline','teacher_dashboard','institute_dashboard','onboarding')), -- Where it shows
  audience text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'all' CHECK (audience IN ('all','parents','students','teachers','institutes')), -- Who sees it
  city_ids uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- Empty = all cities
  deep_link text, -- App route or https URL opened on tap
  priority smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Higher shows first
  starts_at timestamptz NOT NULL, -- Visible from
  ends_at timestamptz, -- Visible until (NULL = until paused)
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','scheduled','active','paused','expired')), -- Lifecycle
  impressions bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Aggregated impressions
  clicks bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Aggregated clicks
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Creator
  updated_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Last editor
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  deleted_at timestamptz, -- Soft delete
  deleted_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Who deleted
  CONSTRAINT ck_banners_window CHECK (ends_at IS NULL OR ends_at > starts_at)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_banners_serving ON banners (placement, audience, priority DESC) WHERE status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_banners_status ON banners (status, starts_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_banners_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON banners FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

Module 45 · Blog Management

Phase 15 · CMS · Depends on: M0, M11 · Owns tables: blogs · Reads: files, admins, classes · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

Articles and guides for parents, students and teachers ("How to choose a Physics tutor for JEE", "CBSE vs ICSE"), shown in the app's Learn tab and on the website. Admins write in Markdown with a preview, attach a cover, tag classes (so parents see content relevant to each child), send drafts for review, schedule, publish and archive.

2. Business Purpose

Content builds trust and brings organic traffic; class-tagged guides make the parent experience feel personal. An editorial workflow keeps quality high.

3. User Stories

  • As a content writer (Operations Admin with blogs.write), I want to save drafts and submit for review so that an editor checks before publishing.
  • As an editor (blogs.publish), I want to schedule a post for 7 AM so that it goes out at the best time.
  • As Operations Admin, I want to tag an article with Class 10 and Class 12 so that parents of those children see it.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-45.1 Workflow. draft → in_review (writer submits) → draft (editor returns with comment) or scheduled / published (editor). published → archived (hidden, URL returns 410 on the website) → draft (restore). Writers can edit only their own drafts; editors can edit anything. Editing a published post creates no new version; changes are live on save (audited with a diff).

FR-45.2 Slug. Generated from the title (lower-case, hyphenated, ≤ 80 chars); unique among non-deleted posts; changing the slug of a published post stores a redirect in settings seo.redirects (website handles 301).

FR-45.3 Rendering. Markdown rendered with markdown-it and sanitised with DOMPurify (server-side for the website, client-side for preview); allowed: headings, lists, links (rel=nofollow for external), images from our CDN only, tables, blockquotes. reading_minutes = ceil(words / 200).

FR-45.4 Scheduling. Job every minute publishes scheduled posts whose published_at ≤ now.

FR-45.5 Personalisation (mobile API). Learn tab: posts whose audience matches and whose class_ids intersect the parent's children's classes (GIN &&), else general posts.

FR-45.6 Views. App/website increment views via events aggregated every 15 minutes into view_count.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
title 10–120 chars
slug ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$, ≤ 80, unique
excerpt ≤ 300 chars; required to publish
contentMd 200–60,000 chars
coverFileId public image, ≥ 1200×630; required to publish
category one of five categories
tags ≤ 10, each 2–30 chars
classIds active class ids
seoTitle / seoDescription ≤ 60 / ≤ 160 chars
publishedAt (schedule) > now, ≤ now + 90 days

GET /blogs/:id blogs.read Detail

PATCH /blogs/:id blogs.write Edit (own drafts; editors any) (If-Match)

Module 46 · Notification Management

Phase 15 · CMS · Depends on: M0, M28, M31 · Owns tables: notifications, notification_recipients · Reads: app_users, files, admins, cities, classes, subscriptions · Build estimate: 4 days

1. Module Overview

Admin-created push and in-app inbox campaigns: to everyone, a role, a segment (city, class, subscription status, last active) or an uploaded user list. Admins compose with a live preview, see the audience size before sending, send now or schedule, and track delivered, failed and opened counts. Large audiences need a second admin's approval. Transactional notifications (lead received, demo reminder) are sent by services and are not managed here.

2. Business Purpose

Direct reach to users for announcements, exam-season campaigns, re-engagement and service messages — with guardrails, because a wrong push to 200,000 families cannot be recalled.

3. User Stories

  • As Operations Admin, I want to notify parents of Class 10 children in Chennai about board-exam teachers so that the message is relevant.
  • As Operations Admin, I want to see how many users will receive the push before sending so that I don't over-send.
  • As Super Admin, I want campaigns to more than 50,000 users to need my approval so that mistakes are caught.
  • As Operations Admin, I want open rates per campaign so that I can improve copy.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-46.1 Lifecycle. draft → (send) → scheduled (if scheduled_at > now) or sending; audiences > 50,000 go to an approval step first (draft stays draft with approval_requested in audit; approver with notifications.approve_large ≠ creator sets approved_by, then it proceeds). sending → sent (or failed if > 50 % failures). scheduled → cancelled any time before send.

FR-46.2 Audience resolution (at send time). SQL built from the segment JSON over app_users (+ joins to parents/students/teachers/institutes, parent_children for class, subscriptions for status); excludes users with notifications opted out, deleted/banned users; target_count stored. user_list accepts ≤ 10,000 ids or a CSV of phones (resolved to ids; unknown phones reported).

FR-46.3 Sending. BullMQ fan-out: insert notification_recipients in chunks of 1,000 (queued), send via FCM sendEach in batches of 500 with each user's device tokens; mark sent / failed (error_code) / no_token; remove UNREGISTERED tokens. Inbox channel writes the message into the user's inbox (served from notification_recipients joined to notifications). Rate: ≤ 2,000 messages/second. Quiet hours: pushes are not delivered 21:30–08:00 IST unless urgent (Super Admin only) — scheduled sends falling in quiet hours are moved to 08:00 with a warning.

FR-46.4 Frequency cap. A user receives at most 2 campaign pushes per 24 h (settings notifications.daily_cap); capped users get inbox only (status = sent, error_code = CAPPED).

FR-46.5 Tracking. App reports opens → opened_at, opened_count. Counters are updated by the worker with UPDATE … SET delivered_count = delivered_count + $n.

FR-46.6 Test send. POST /notifications/:id/test { adminDeviceUserIds[] } sends to up to 5 test accounts without changing state.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
title 3–60 chars
body 5–180 chars
imageFileId public image 2:1, ≤ 300 KB
deepLink registry route (same list as Module 44)
channel push, inbox, push_and_inbox
audienceType all, parents, students, teachers, institutes, segment, user_list
segment allowed keys: cityIds, classIds, roles, subscriptionStatus, lastActiveWithinDays (1–365), inactiveForDays (1–365), hasChildren
userIds ≤ 10,000 uuids
scheduledAt > now + 5 min, ≤ now + 30 days

GET /notifications/:id notifications.read Detail with stats

PATCH /notifications/:id notifications.send Edit draft (If-Match)

9. PostgreSQL Tables

notifications

Push / in-app notification campaigns created by admins (transactional pushes are sent by services and not stored here).

CREATE TABLE notifications (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  title text NOT NULL, -- Max 60 chars
  body text NOT NULL, -- Max 180 chars
  image_file_id uuid REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Optional rich image
  deep_link text, -- App route opened on tap
  channel text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'push_and_inbox' CHECK (channel IN ('push','inbox','push_and_inbox')), -- Delivery channel
  audience_type text NOT NULL CHECK (audience_type IN ('all','parents','students','teachers','institutes','segment','user_list')), -- Who receives it
  segment jsonb, -- Filters for audience_type = segment, e.g. {"city_ids":[…],"class_ids":[…],"subscription_status":["trial"]}
  user_ids uuid[], -- Explicit recipients for audience_type = user_list (max 10,000)
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','scheduled','sending','sent','failed','cancelled')), -- Lifecycle
  scheduled_at timestamptz, -- Send time (NULL = send now)
  sent_at timestamptz, -- Finished sending
  target_count integer, -- Recipients resolved at send time
  delivered_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- FCM success count
  failed_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- FCM failures
  opened_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Opens reported by the app
  created_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Creator
  approved_by uuid REFERENCES admins(id), -- Second admin approval for audiences over 50,000
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Created
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Updated
  deleted_at timestamptz -- Soft delete (drafts only)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notifications_status ON notifications (status, scheduled_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_notifications_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON notifications FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

notification_recipients

Per-user delivery record for a campaign. Partition by month at scale.

CREATE TABLE notification_recipients (
  notification_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES notifications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Campaign
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Recipient
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (status IN ('queued','sent','failed','opened','no_token')), -- Delivery state
  error_code text, -- FCM error, e.g. UNREGISTERED
  sent_at timestamptz, -- Sent
  opened_at timestamptz, -- Opened
  PRIMARY KEY (notification_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notification_recipients_user ON notification_recipients (user_id, sent_at DESC);

Module 47 · Dashboard Analytics

Phase 16 · Reporting · Depends on: M16–M46 (reads their tables) · Owns tables: daily_platform_stats · Reads: teachers, institutes, parents, students, subscriptions, transactions, leads, demo_requests, teacher_reviews, complaints, trust_scores · Build estimate: 4 days

1. Module Overview

The admin home: KPI cards (teachers, verified teachers, pending approvals, institutes, parents, students, active subscriptions, revenue, average trust score), trend charts, a city breakdown, and action queues (pending approvals, flagged reviews, SLA-breaching complaints, held refunds). Historical numbers come from daily_platform_stats, written by a nightly job and refreshed hourly for today, so the dashboard loads fast regardless of data size.

2. Business Purpose

Gives leadership and each admin role an at-a-glance picture of platform health and — more usefully — tells each admin what needs their attention now.

3. User Stories

  • As Super Admin, I want revenue, sign-ups and active subscriptions for the last 30 days compared to the previous 30 so that I can see momentum.
  • As Verification Admin, I want my pending queue counts on the home page so that I start where I'm needed.
  • As Operations Admin, I want a city breakdown of parents, students and teachers so that I can find supply gaps.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-47.1 Stats job. Nightly at 00:30 IST computes the previous day's row (ON CONFLICT (stat_date) DO UPDATE); hourly recomputes today. Totals are end-of-day snapshots; new_* are counts created that day (IST); revenue_paise = captured − refunded processed that day; city_breakdown per city id. Backfill command npm run stats:backfill -- --from=2026-01-01.

FR-47.2 KPIs. GET /dashboard/summary?range=7d|30d|90d|custom returns each KPI's current value, value at range start, delta %, and a sparkline series from daily_platform_stats. Pending counts (teachers, institutes, documents, reviews, complaints, refunds) are live queries (cheap, indexed partial queues).

FR-47.3 Role-aware widgets. The API returns only widgets the admin's permissions allow (e.g. revenue requires reports.revenue; queues require the related read permission). The UI renders what it receives.

FR-47.4 Charts. Sign-ups by role (stacked area), revenue (bar, by purpose from transactions for ≤ 90 days), leads → demos → conversions funnel, trust score distribution (from Module 36), city table.

FR-47.5 Caching. Responses cached in Redis 5 min per (range, permission set hash); a "Refresh" button bypasses cache (rate-limited 1/min per admin).

FR-47.6 Timezone. All day boundaries in Asia/Kolkata.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
range 7d, 30d, 90d, 12m or custom
from / to required for custom; ≤ 366 days; to ≤ today
cityId active city (optional filter for city-scoped widgets)

Module 48 · Revenue Reports

Phase 16 · Reporting · Depends on: M40, M41 (report_exports is shared by M49 and M50) · Owns tables: report_exports · Reads: transactions, refunds, subscriptions, payment_configurations, files, admins · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

Finance-grade revenue reporting: gross, refunds and net revenue by day/week/month, by purpose and fee code, by payer type and city; GST summary for filing; subscription MRR and renewals; and a transaction-level ledger export. Also owns the shared asynchronous export system (report_exports) used by every report module.

2. Business Purpose

Finance needs numbers that tie out to Razorpay settlements and GST returns, exportable for the accountant, without running SQL against production.

3. User Stories

  • As Finance Admin, I want monthly net revenue by fee code so that I can see which products earn.
  • As Finance Admin, I want a GST summary (taxable value, GST collected, credit notes) by month and state so that I can file GSTR-1/3B.
  • As Finance Admin, I want to export a month's ledger to Excel so that the accountant can reconcile.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-48.1 Definitions. Gross = sum of amount_paise of transactions captured in the period (direction credit). Refunds = sum of processed refunds in the period (by processed_at). Net = Gross − Refunds. Taxable value = base amounts; GST = gst_paise; referral payouts (debit) are reported separately as marketing cost, never subtracted from revenue. All grouping by IST date.

FR-48.2 Reports.

Report Endpoint Grouping
Revenue overview /reports/revenue/overview granularity day/week/month; series gross, refunds, net; totals and period-over-period
By product /reports/revenue/by-product fee code and purpose; count, gross, refunds, net, average price
By segment /reports/revenue/by-segment payer type, city, state
GST summary /reports/revenue/gst month × place-of-supply state: taxable value, CGST/SGST (intra-state, Karnataka) or IGST, credit notes
Subscriptions /reports/revenue/subscriptions MRR trend, new/renewed/churned subscriptions, ARPU
Ledger /reports/revenue/ledger transaction-level rows (paginated)

FR-48.3 Exports (shared by M48–M50). POST /report-exports { reportType, filters, format } → queued; BullMQ worker streams rows from a read-only connection with a server-side cursor (pg-query-stream) to CSV or XLSX (exceljs streaming writer), uploads to the private bucket, sets completed, row_count, file_id, expires_at = now + 7 days, notifies the requester in-app. Max 1,000,000 rows; max 3 concurrent exports per admin. Download via GET /report-exports/:id/download (presigned 60 s). Cleanup job deletes expired files and sets expired.

FR-48.4 Consistency. Reports read from the primary until a read replica exists; each response includes asOf time. Money totals are computed in SQL (sum(bigint)), never in JS floats.

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
from / to required; to ≥ from; ≤ 366 days (ledger ≤ 92 days on screen, any range ≤ 366 days for export)
granularity day (≤ 92 days), week, month
feeCode / purpose / payerType / cityId / stateId valid values
export.reportType allowed for the requester's permissions (revenue types need reports.revenue)
export.format csv or xlsx

9. PostgreSQL Tables

report_exports

Asynchronous CSV/XLSX exports for all report modules. Files expire after 7 days.

CREATE TABLE report_exports (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  report_type text NOT NULL CHECK (report_type IN ('revenue','transactions','subscriptions','teachers','teacher_performance','institutes','institute_ratings','leads','reviews','complaints','referrals','audit_logs')), -- Which report
  filters jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb, -- Filters used, e.g. {"from":"2026-09-01","to":"2026-09-30","city_id":"…"}
  format text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'csv' CHECK (format IN ('csv','xlsx')), -- Output format
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','completed','failed','expired')), -- Job state
  row_count integer, -- Rows written
  file_id uuid REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Output file (private)
  error text, -- Failure reason
  requested_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admins(id), -- Requester
  started_at timestamptz, -- Job start
  completed_at timestamptz, -- Job end
  expires_at timestamptz, -- Download link expiry
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Requested
);
CREATE INDEX idx_report_exports_requester ON report_exports (requested_by, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_report_exports_status ON report_exports (status, created_at);

Module 49 · Teacher Reports

Phase 16 · Reporting · Depends on: M16–M21, M33, M36, M38, M39, M41, M48 (exports) · Owns tables: none · Reads: teachers, teacher_documents, teacher_subjects, teacher_locations, teacher_daily_stats, leads, demo_requests, teacher_reviews, trust_scores, subscriptions, complaints, report_exports · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Overview

Operational and quality reports about teachers: supply (by city, subject, class, mode), onboarding funnel and verification turnaround, performance (views, leads, response rate, demos, conversions, ratings, trust), paid products (premium/featured uptake), and risk (complaints, low trust). Owns no tables — it reads module tables and teacher_daily_stats and uses the shared export system from Module 48.

2. Business Purpose

Operations decides where to recruit teachers, whom to promote, and whom to coach or remove. These decisions need consistent, exportable numbers rather than ad-hoc queries.

3. User Stories

  • As Operations Admin, I want subject × city supply versus parent demand so that I can recruit where parents can't find teachers.
  • As Verification Admin, I want average approval turnaround and rejection reasons so that I can improve the process.
  • As Operations Admin, I want the top and bottom 50 teachers by response rate and conversion so that I can reward or coach them.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-49.1 Reports.

Report Endpoint Content
Supply /reports/teachers/supply approved teachers by city × subject (or class, mode, category); demand = parent children needing that subject/class in the city (Module 29); gap ratio = demand ÷ supply
Onboarding funnel /reports/teachers/onboarding signed up → profile complete → documents submitted → paid → approved; drop-off %; median time per step
Verification /reports/teachers/verification decisions per day, median/p90 turnaround (submitted → decision), rejection reasons, per-verifier throughput
Performance /reports/teachers/performance per teacher: profile views, leads, response rate 24 h, median response, demos, no-shows, conversions, rating, reviews, trust score; sortable, with percentiles
Paid products /reports/teachers/products premium/featured purchases, active count, renewal rate, performance lift (leads per day before vs during)
Risk /reports/teachers/risk teachers with trust < 60, upheld complaints, many declines, no-shows ≥ 2 in 30 days, suspended

FR-49.2 Data sources. Daily counters (teacher_daily_stats: views, leads, contacts, demos) are summed for performance; statuses and ratings come from current rows; turnarounds from teacher_verification_logs.

FR-49.3 Thresholds. Performance report hides teachers with < 5 leads in the period from rate rankings (shown with "not enough data").

FR-49.4 Drill-down. Every teacher row links to the teacher page (Module 17) with the same date range applied to its Analytics tab (Module 21).

FR-49.5 Export. All reports exportable via Module 48 (reportType teachers or teacher_performance).

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
from / to required; ≤ 366 days
dimension (supply) subject, class, mode, category
cityId / subjectId / classId / categoryId valid ids
minLeads (performance) 0–1,000, default 5
sort (performance) leads, responseRate, conversionRate, rating, trustScore, views

GET /reports/teachers/products reports.teachers Premium / featured
GET /reports/teachers/risk reports.teachers Risk list

  • SupplyHeatmap — city × subject grid coloured by gap ratio with a legend and numeric values in cells (not colour alone).

16. Filters

Date range, city, area, subject, class, teaching mode, category, verified badge, premium/featured, trust band.

17. Search Capabilities

Teacher name/code on Performance and Risk tabs.

18. Pagination Requirements

Performance and Risk: offset, default 50, max 100. Supply, funnel, verification, products: aggregates (no pagination; supply capped at 500 rows, sorted by gap).

19. Audit Logs

Read-only; exports and downloads are audited by Module 48.

21. Future Scalability Notes & Enhancements

Recruitment targets per city; teacher cohort retention; NPS by teacher; automatic coaching nudges for low responders.

Module 50 · Institute Reports

Phase 16 · Reporting · Depends on: M22–M27, M34, M38, M41, M48 (exports) · Owns tables: none · Reads: institutes, institute_documents, institute_verification_logs, institute_ratings, institute_teachers, institute_batches, institute_reviews, leads, subscriptions, complaints, report_exports · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Overview

Reports about institutes: onboarding and verification funnel, rating distribution and criteria scores, lead and enquiry performance, batches and capacity, teacher counts, subscription status and risk. Owns no tables; uses the shared export system from Module 48.

2. Business Purpose

Institutes are a newer, higher-value segment. Operations needs to see verification speed, rating quality and whether institutes get enough enquiries to renew.

3. User Stories

  • As Verification Admin, I want the distribution of institute ratings and the average of each criterion so that ratings stay calibrated between evaluators.
  • As Operations Admin, I want enquiries per institute per month and response rate so that I can help institutes that don't respond.
  • As Finance Admin, I want institutes whose registration expires in the next 30 days with their lead counts so that renewal calls are informed.

4. Functional Requirements & Business Logic

FR-50.1 Reports.

Report Endpoint Content
Onboarding & verification /reports/institutes/onboarding draft → submitted → under evaluation → approved/rejected counts, median turnaround, rejection reasons, per-evaluator throughput
Ratings /reports/institutes/ratings distribution of overall_rating (0.5 buckets), criterion averages, evaluator calibration (each evaluator's mean vs overall mean, override frequency)
Performance /reports/institutes/performance per institute: page views, leads, response rate, median response, campus visits, conversions, user rating, reviews, teachers, active batches
Capacity /reports/institutes/capacity batches by subject/class/mode, seats, fill rate (enrolled ÷ capacity where tracked)
Renewals /reports/institutes/renewals registrations expiring in N days with last-90-day leads and conversions
Risk /reports/institutes/risk upheld complaints, rating ≤ 2.5, suspended, response rate < 50 %

FR-50.2 Calibration. Evaluator mean deviation > 0.5 stars from the overall mean (min 10 ratings) is highlighted for Super Admin review.

FR-50.3 Drill-down. Rows link to the institute page (Module 24) with the date range applied.

FR-50.4 Export. Via Module 48 (reportType institutes or institute_ratings).

5. Validation Rules

Field Rule
from / to required; ≤ 366 days
expiringInDays (renewals) 7, 15, 30, 60, 90
cityId / subjectId / classId valid ids
minRatings (calibration) 1–100, default 10

GET /reports/institutes/renewals reports.institutes Upcoming renewals
